- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. ## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- vercel:bootstrap: Project bootstrapping orchestrator for repos that depend on Vercel-linked resources (databases, auth, and managed integrations). Use when setting up or repairing a repository so linking, environment provisioning, env pulls, and first-run db/dev commands happen in the correct safe order.
- vercel:chat-sdk: Vercel Chat SDK expert guidance. Use when building multi-platform chat bots — Slack, Telegram, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Google Chat, GitHub, Linear — with a single codebase. Covers the Chat class, adapters, threads, messages, cards, modals, streaming, state management, and webhook setup.
- vercel:deployments-cicd: Vercel deployment and CI/CD expert guidance. Use when deploying, promoting, rolling back, inspecting deployments, building with --prebuilt, or configuring CI workflow files for Vercel.
- vercel:env-vars: Vercel environment variable expert guidance. Use when working with .env files, vercel env commands, OIDC tokens, or managing environment-specific configuration.
- vercel:knowledge-update: Corrects outdated LLM knowledge about the Vercel platform and introduces new products. Injected at session start.
- vercel:marketplace: Vercel Marketplace expert guidance — discovering, installing, and managing integrations via the `vercel integration` CLI, with auto-provisioned environment variables and unified billing. Use when consuming third-party services on Vercel.
- vercel:microfrontends: Guide for building, configuring, and deploying microfrontends on Vercel. Use this skill when the user mentions microfrontends, multi-zones, splitting an app across teams, independent deployments, cross-app routing, incremental migration, composing multiple frontends under one domain, microfrontends.json, @vercel/microfrontends, the microfrontends local proxy, or path-based routing between Vercel projects. Also use when the user asks about shared layouts across projects, navigation between microfrontends, fallback environments, asset prefixes, or feature flag controlled routing.
- vercel:next-cache-components: Next.js 16 Cache Components guidance — PPR, use cache directive, cacheLife, cacheTag, updateTag, and migration from unstable_cache. Use when implementing partial prerendering, caching strategies, or migrating from older Next.js cache patterns.
- vercel:next-forge: next-forge expert guidance — production-grade Turborepo monorepo SaaS starter by Vercel. Use when working in a next-forge project, scaffolding with `npx next-forge init`, or editing @repo/* workspace packages.
- vercel:next-upgrade: Upgrade Next.js to the latest version following official migration guides and codemods. Use when upgrading Next.js versions, running codemods, or migrating between major releases.
- vercel:nextjs: Next.js App Router expert guidance. Use when building, debugging, or architecting Next.js applications — routing, Server Components, Server Actions, Cache Components, layouts, middleware/proxy, data fetching, rendering strategies, and deployment on Vercel.
- vercel:react-best-practices: React best-practices reviewer for TSX files. Triggers after editing multiple TSX components to run a condensed quality checklist covering component structure, hooks usage, accessibility, performance, and TypeScript patterns.
- vercel:routing-middleware: Vercel Routing Middleware guidance — request interception before cache, rewrites, redirects, personalization. Works with any framework. Supports Edge, Node.js, and Bun runtimes. Use when intercepting requests at the platform level.
- vercel:runtime-cache: Vercel Runtime Cache API guidance — ephemeral per-region key-value cache with tag-based invalidation. Shared across Functions, Routing Middleware, and Builds. Use when implementing caching strategies beyond framework-level caching.
- vercel:shadcn: shadcn/ui expert guidance — CLI, component installation, composition patterns, custom registries, theming, Tailwind CSS integration, and high-quality interface design. Use when initializing shadcn, adding components, composing product UI, building custom registries, configuring themes, or troubleshooting component issues.
- vercel:turbopack: Turbopack expert guidance. Use when configuring the Next.js bundler, optimizing HMR, debugging build issues, or understanding the Turbopack vs Webpack differences.
- vercel:vercel-agent: Vercel Agent guidance — AI-powered code review, incident investigation, and SDK installation. Automates PR analysis and anomaly debugging. Use when configuring or understanding Vercel's AI development tools.
- vercel:vercel-cli: Vercel CLI expert guidance. Use when deploying, managing environment variables, linking projects, viewing logs, querying metrics, managing domains, or interacting with the Vercel platform from the command line.
- vercel:vercel-connect: Vercel Connect expert guidance — securely obtain scoped OAuth tokens for third-party services (Slack, GitHub, MCP servers, OAuth, Snowflake) on behalf of apps or users via Vercel OIDC. Use when wiring up third-party API access, connecting to MCP servers, sending Slack messages, accessing GitHub APIs, receiving webhook events from Slack/Linear/GitHub and forwarding them to your agents and apps, or building Eve agent connections.
- vercel:vercel-firewall: Vercel Firewall expert guidance — automatic DDoS mitigation, the Vercel WAF (custom rules, IP blocking, managed rulesets, rate limiting), Attack Mode, system bypass, bot management, and the `vercel firewall` CLI. Use when configuring platform-level security, responding to attacks, or staging firewall rules.
- vercel:vercel-functions: Vercel Functions expert guidance — Serverless Functions, Edge Functions, Fluid Compute, streaming, Cron Jobs, and runtime configuration. Use when configuring, debugging, or optimizing server-side code running on Vercel.
- vercel:vercel-sandbox: Vercel Sandbox guidance — ephemeral Firecracker microVMs for running untrusted code safely. Supports AI agents, code generation, and experimentation. Use when executing user-generated or AI-generated code in isolation.
- vercel:vercel-storage: Vercel storage expert guidance — Blob, Edge Config, and Marketplace storage (Neon Postgres, Upstash Redis). Use when choosing, configuring, or using data storage with Vercel applications.
- vercel:verification: Full-story verification — infers what the user is building, then verifies the complete flow end-to-end: browser → API → data → response. Triggers on dev server start and 'why isn't this working' signals.
- vercel:workflow: Vercel Workflow DevKit (WDK) expert guidance. Use when building durable workflows, long-running tasks, API routes or agents that need pause/resume, retries, step-based execution, or crash-safe orchestration with Vercel Workflow.
- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use when: morning brief, daily brief, set up my morning brief, what's my day look like, run my brief.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

I have a comprehensive picture of the codebase. Here is my structured summary.

---

# Zimmermann PWA — Commerce API Surface (for the MRT/SFCC spike)

## 1. Framework & versions

This **is** a PWA Kit storefront, built via **template extensibility** on top of Salesforce's `retail-react-app`. Notably, the `@salesforce/*` packages are NOT direct `dependencies` — they come in through the extended base template, so you must resolve them from `node_modules`.

- `package.json:17-20` — `ccExtensibility: { extends: "@salesforce/retail-react-app", overridesDir: "overrides" }`. Overrides live in `/overrides/app`.
- `package.json:13-16` — node engine `^18 || ^20 || ^22 || ^24`, npm `^9 || ^10 || ^11`.
- `package.json:23` — `@salesforce/retail-react-app: 10.0.0` (in **devDependencies**).

Installed versions resolved from `node_modules`:
| Package | Version |
|---|---|
| `@salesforce/retail-react-app` | **10.0.0** |
| `@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime` | **3.18.0** |
| `@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk` | **3.18.0** |
| `@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev` | **3.18.0** |
| `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` | **5.2.0** (transitive; the actual Shopper-API client) |
| `react` / `react-dom` | **18.3.1** |

Note: `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react-preview` and `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-isomorphic` are NOT present as top-level installs — the current package is `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (v5.2.0). Direct `dependencies` in `package.json:113-117` are only Contentful (`@contentful/experiences-sdk-react`, `@contentful/live-preview`, `contentful`).

## 2. Managed Runtime config

Main config: `config/default.js`. SSR entrypoint: `overrides/app/ssr.js`.

**Proxy configuration** (`config/default.js:206-218`, `ssrParameters.proxyConfigs`):
- `path: 'api'` → host `qmyt7hks.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com` — this is **SCAPI** (shortCode `qmyt7hks`). Reached at `/mobify/proxy/api`.
- `path: 'ocapi'` → host `bkzk-002.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com` — **OCAPI** on the dev sandbox.
- `config/default.js:207` — `ssrFunctionNodeVersion: '24.x'`.
- Commerce API proxyPath declared at `config/default.js:131` — `proxyPath: '/mobify/proxy/api'`.

**SSR settings** (`overrides/app/ssr.js`):
- `defaultCacheTimeSeconds: 600` (`ssr.js:29`).
- `port: 3000` (`ssr.js:35`).
- `useSLASPrivateClient: true` (`ssr.js:52`) — SLAS **private-client** flow, requires `PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET`.
- `localAllowCookies: false` (`ssr.js:80`).
- `hybridProxy.enabled: false` (`ssr.js:91-114`) — Hybrid Proxy / MRT-to-ODS routing rules are present but disabled (dev-only tooling; production expects eCDN).
- Custom Express routes: `/callback`, JWKS caching (`/:shortCode/:tenantId/oauth2/jwks`), passwordless & reset-password SLAS callbacks, `/api/payment-metadata`, service worker (`ssr.js:135-187`).
- `config/default.js:198` — `ssrEnabled: true`.

**App origin** is resolved at runtime via `getAppOrigin()` from `@salesforce/pwa-kit-react-sdk/utils/url` — see `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx:30,113`. The proxy and SLAS-private-client endpoints are built as `${appOrigin}${getEnvBasePath()}${proxyPath}` (`_app-config/index.tsx:126-129`).

## 3. Commerce API configuration (clientId / org / shortCode / siteId / realm)

Configured in `config/default.js:129-138` via env vars, injected into the SDK provider:
```
commerceAPI.parameters = {
  clientId:       process.env.COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID,
  organizationId: process.env.COMMERCE_API_ORGANIZATION_ID,
  shortCode:      process.env.COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE,
  siteId:         process.env.COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID,
}
```
These are passed to `<CommerceApiProvider>` in `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx:132-151`.

Actual values (from `.env`, currently pointed at **dev**):
- `COMMERCE_API_SHORT_CODE=qmyt7hks` (`.env:11`) — real, non-placeholder.
- `COMMERCE_API_ORGANIZATION_ID=f_ecom_bkzk_002` (`.env:9`) — real (realm/instance `bkzk_002`).
- `COMMERCE_API_SITE_ID=ZimmermannAU` (`.env:12`) — real default site.
- `COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID=c2ab1fe0-...eb1c` (`.env:13`) — real-looking SLAS client UUID.
- `COMMERCE_API_OCAPI_HOST=bkzk-002.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com` (`.env:8`) — dev sandbox OCAPI host.
- `COMMERCE_API_SCAPI_HOST=` (`.env:10`) — blank (SCAPI reached via shortCode host, not this var).
- `PWA_KIT_SLAS_CLIENT_SECRET=BH4rPHR...` (`.env:14`) — **a real-looking SLAS private-client secret is committed in `.env`** (flag this; secrets policy in `.env.sample:53-62` says secrets should live only in `.env`/MRT).

Placeholder/template contrast: `.env.sample:65` shows `COMMERCE_API_OCAPI_HOST=TODO` and `COMMERCE_API_ORGANIZATION_ID=TODO` — confirming `.env` holds resolved dev values while `.env.sample` is the scaffold.

**SCAPI vs OCAPI:** Primary path is **SCAPI (Shopper APIs) via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`**. OCAPI is proxied only as a fallback for operations "not yet covered by SCAPI" (`.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md:52`). The `api` proxy is SCAPI; the `ocapi` proxy is the legacy fallback. `scripts/sfcc/syncRegionalConfig.mjs:9-10` explicitly notes SCAPI is "the current, non-deprecated successor to OCAPI's Data API."

## 4. Data fetching (product / category / pricing)

All commerce data uses **`@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hooks** (TanStack Query under the hood). The base retail-react-app supplies the PDP/PLP; the overrides use hooks directly in Contentful-driven components:

- **Products:** `useProduct` — `overrides/app/components/contentful/productHero.tsx:4,16` (fetches product with `allImages: true`), and `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/hotspotPopup.tsx:3,12`.
- **Search + pricing:** `useProductSearch` — `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:36,52`. This is the richest example of the pricing/category surface:
  ```
  refine: ['cgid=<categoryId>', 'htype=master'],
  expand: ['promotions','variations','prices','images','custom_properties'],
  perPricebook: true,
  allVariationProperties: true,
  ```
  (`home/index.tsx:53-60`) — i.e. category refinement via `cgid`, price-book-aware pricing (`perPricebook`), promotions and variation expansion.
- **Auth/customer:** `useAuthHelper`, `useCustomerType`, `AuthHelpers` — `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx:26`.
- **Provider setup:** `CommerceApiProvider` + `withReactQuery` in `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx:27-28,132-160`; query defaults (staleTime 10s, retry off) at `:222-236`.

No GraphQL and no custom REST product client — SFCC access is exclusively through the SDK hooks.

**MuleSoft integration point (relevant to "MRT API capabilities"):** There is a **direct PWA → MRT → MuleSoft** read path documented and partially scaffolded, but **not yet wired into `proxyConfigs`**:
- Undici connection pool exists: `overrides/app/ssr/connectionPools.ts:42-46` — `mulesoftPool` (`MULESOFT_BASE_URL`, 20 connections). Same file also defines pools for SCAPI (`sfccScapiPool:22`), SF Payments, Marketing Cloud, Google Places, and Booxi.
- Intended proxy path `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...` is described in `.env.sample:139-152` and `.docs/integration/03-mulesoft.md:5,38,44`, but **no `mulesoft` entry exists in any `config/*.js proxyConfigs`** (grep of `config/` for `mulesoft` returns nothing) — so this path is designed but not yet implemented.
- MuleSoft covers order history, order detail, returns, real-time boutique/BOPIS stock, and GiveX balance (`.docs/integration/03-mulesoft.md:61-76`). **Product/pricing master data is explicitly out of scope for the PWA** — the AP21 → MuleSoft → SFCC catalogue/pricebook feed is server-to-server (`03-mulesoft.md:24-25`). So for the spike: product, category, and pricing all come from **SCAPI**, not MuleSoft.
- `package.json:83` — `test:contracts` is a stubbed TODO awaiting the MuleSoft OpenAPI spec.

Keyword grep results (`overrides`, `scripts`, `config`, `.docs`): `MRT`/"managed runtime" appear in `ssr.js:82-104`, `scripts/smokeTest.js` (uses `MRT_URL`), `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts:8,36`; `scapi`/`ocapi` appear across `config/*.js`, `scripts/sfcc/*.mjs`, and the docs.

## 5. Environments / lower environments

Extensive multi-tier setup:
- Env-specific runtime configs: `config/dev.js`, `config/test.js`, `config/sit.js`, `config/staging.js`, `config/uat.js`, `config/production.js` — each overrides `proxyConfigs` (differing OCAPI host; SCAPI host stays `qmyt7hks...`). Example: `config/production.js:13-15` points OCAPI at `production-ap01-zimmermann.demandware.net`; `config/dev.js:13-15` at `bkzk-002.dx...`.
- Per-tier env files at repo root: `.env.dev`, `.env.test`, `.env.sit`, `.env.staging`, `.env.uat`, `.env.prod`, plus `.env.shared` and the template `.env.sample`.
- Env switcher tooling: `scripts/switchEnv.mjs` + `npm run env` (`package.json:87`); the active `.env:1-2` is marked "Generated by `npm run env -- dev`", `DEPLOY_TARGET=dev`.
- Deploy scripts per tier: `push:dev|test|sit|staging|uat|prod` (`package.json:76-81`) → `pwa-kit-dev push -t <target>`.
- SFCC realm is a sandbox (`bkzk-002` / org `f_ecom_bkzk_002`); production OCAPI host is `production-ap01-zimmermann.demandware.net`. `.env.sample:44` header references the "BKZK-001 instance."
- Validation/live-check tooling described in `.env.sample:20-40` (real SLAS guest token + Contentful Delivery calls per tier).

## 6. Contentful / CMS

Contentful is the CMS and is a **direct `dependencies` entry** (unlike the SFCC packages). It is a content layer that *references* SFCC products by ID; it does not carry product/pricing data itself.

- Config: `config/default.js:184-191` — `spaceId`, `accessToken` (delivery), `environment`, `previewAccessToken`, all from env. `.env:30-35` has real dev values (space `u9kb6gp6slxu`, env `dev`, delivery + preview + management tokens committed).
- Provider: `ContentfulLivePreviewProvider` wraps the app in `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx:43,154`.
- **Relationship to product data:** Contentful entries hold a product ID (a string), and the component then fetches live commerce data from SFCC via the SDK. Clearest example: `productHero.tsx` receives `productHero: string` (an SKU/ID) as a Contentful field and calls `useProduct({ parameters: { id: productHero }})` (`productHero.tsx:8,13,16`). Same pattern in `experiences/hotspotPopup.tsx`. So Contentful = merchandising/layout; SFCC SCAPI = product/category/pricing truth.
- Contentful env IDs are mapped per MRT tier via `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` (`overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts:8,36`). Tooling: `sync:contentful`, `setup:contentful`, `migrate:contentful`, `generate:contentful` (`package.json:66-71,84`), plus `@contentful/experiences-sdk-react` for Experience Builder.

## Key files for the spike
- `config/default.js` — commerce API params, proxies, feature flags (`:129-218`).
- `overrides/app/ssr.js` — MRT/SSR server, SLAS private client, hybrid proxy rules.
- `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx` — `CommerceApiProvider` wiring, multi-site/locale resolution.
- `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:52-60` — canonical product-search + pricing query shape.
- `overrides/app/ssr/connectionPools.ts` — SSR upstream pools (SCAPI, MuleSoft, etc.).
- `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` — SCAPI endpoint inventory (`:69-80`), auth, multi-region.
- `.docs/integration/03-mulesoft.md` — the direct PWA→MRT→MuleSoft read path (not for product/pricing).

**Things explicitly NOT present:** no `mobify` block in `package.json` (config lives in `config/*.js` instead); no `mulesoft` proxy entry in any `config/*.js` (only `api`/SCAPI and `ocapi`); no GraphQL or custom product API client; MuleSoft does not serve product/category/pricing to the PWA.

Keyword grep results (`overrides`, `scripts`, `config`, `.docs`): `MRT`/"managed runtime" appear in `ssr.js:82-104`, `scripts/smokeTest.js` (uses `MRT_URL`), `overrides/app/config/contentfulMapping.ts:8,36`; `scapi`/`ocapi` appear across `config/*.js`, `scripts/sfcc/*.mjs`, and the docs.

Extensive multi-tier setup:

- Deploy scripts per tier: `push:dev|test|sit|staging|uat|prod` (`package.json:76-81`) → `pwa-kit-dev push -t <target>`.
- SFCC realm is a sandbox (`bkzk-002` / org `f_ecom_bkzk_002`); production OCAPI host is `production-ap01-zimmermann.demandware.net`. `.env.sample:44` header references the "BKZK-001 instance."

- Config: `config/default.js:184-191` — `spaceId`, `accessToken` (delivery), `environment`, `previewAccessToken`, all from env. `.env:30-35` has real dev values (space `u9kb6gp6slxu`, env `dev`, delivery + preview + management tokens committed).

- `overrides/app/ssr.js` — MRT/SSR server, SLAS private client, hybrid proxy rules.

- `.docs/integration/03-mulesoft.md` — the direct PWA→MRT→MuleSoft read path (not for product/pricing).

**Things explicitly NOT present:** no `mobify` block in `package.json` (config lives in `config/*.js` instead); no `mulesoft` proxy entry in any `config/*.js` (only `api`/SCAPI and `ocapi`); no GraphQL or custom product API client; MuleSoft does not serve product/category/pricing to the PWA.

1	# 01 — Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SCAPI) + reCAPTCHA
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	Salesforce Commerce Cloud B2C (SFCC) is the system of record for commerce data. The storefront calls SFCC directly from the browser via SCAPI for browsing, basket management, customer accounts, and order placement.
6	
7	In scope:
8	
9	- Authentication via Shopper Login & API Access Service (SLAS)
10	- Product catalogue, categories, search, recommendations
11	- Basket and cart
12	- Customer account (authentication record) and saved-payment token references
13	- Order placement for SFCC-owned checkouts (domestic markets)
14	- Gift cards — the storefront applies them via SCAPI; server-side redemption is outside the PWA boundary
15	- Google reCAPTCHA — browser-side script load on register/login forms; MRT-side token verification before SCAPI submission
16	
17	At migration, only the customer's email and Omneo ID are stored in SFCC. Name, phone, addresses, and communication preferences come from Omneo at login (DMU-004). Order history comes from MuleSoft via the MRT proxy, not from SFCC (DMU-007).
18	
19	Out of scope of this document:
20	
21	- GiveX validate/redeem/refund, Avalara tax, Adyen back-office — all server-side, outside the PWA
22	- SFCC ↔ MuleSoft flows to NewStore, AP21, Omneo, Narvar
23	- Booxi appointment booking — MRT-mediated (PWA → MRT → Booxi), not a SFCC flow
24	- Business Manager configuration: promotions rules, content slots, Page Designer pages
25	
26	## 2. Browser-side architecture
27	
28	```
29	PWA (React, SSR + CSR)
30	        │
31	        │  @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react (TanStack Query under the hood)
32	        ▼
33	SLAS auth (guest or registered shopper) ──► Shopper context
34	        │                                       (site, currency, locale, customer)
35	        ▼
36	SCAPI: products, search, baskets, orders, customers, promotions, gift cards
37	        │
38	        ▼
39	SFCC realm
40	```
41	
42	- **Single SDK.** `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` handles every SFCC call — SLAS token lifecycle, retry, and TanStack Query caching.
43	- **SSR and CSR.** Catalogue, PDP, PLP, content, and boutique pages are server-rendered for SEO and LCP. Cart, checkout, My Account, and order pages render an SSR shell and hydrate personalised data client-side after auth.
44	- **Managed Runtime.** The PWA Kit Node layer hosts the SSR pipeline and routes SLAS private-client calls through the server-side proxy.
45	
46	## 3. Authentication and credentials
47	
48	- **SLAS private-client flow** issues two token types: a guest access token (anonymous shopper, refreshed silently) and a registered shopper access token (issued after email/password login). Tokens are JWTs with a customer ID, unique shopper ID (USID), and refresh token.
49	- **Refresh tokens live in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies** set by the SSR layer. Browser JavaScript never sees the raw refresh token. On each refresh SLAS regenerates the token and voids the old one; the SSR layer rewrites the cookie in the same response.
50	- **Private client credentials.** The SLAS client secret is an MRT environment variable and never reaches the browser. The authorisation code exchange goes through the MRT private-client proxy (`privateClientProxyEndpoint`). The SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code stay in the bundle as public identifiers.
51	- **Social login.** Apple and Google via SLAS third-party identity-provider federation — confirmed in scope for launch; implementation design still open.
52	- **No Open Commerce API (OCAPI) credentials in the browser.** Any operation not yet covered by SCAPI is proxied through Managed Runtime with OCAPI credentials held server-side.
53	
54	### Magento password migration (CFD-013)
55	
56	Passwords were not migrated from Magento. All existing customers must reset at go-live. Failed sign-ins return a generic "invalid credentials" message (no email-existence leak) and the "forgot password" link is always visible.
57	
58	### Cross-storefront session continuity
59	
60	All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single domain and share one SFCC realm.
61	
62	- **The refresh-token cookie is shared across storefronts.** Every storefront lives on the same domain, so the `httpOnly` cookie is sent on every path prefix. No cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.
63	- **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A token issued for `zimm-au` is not valid for `zimm-uk` — this is a hard SLAS platform constraint. On a storefront switch the SSR layer performs a fresh authorisation for the destination channel using the SLAS Trusted System on Behalf (TSOB) flow: it calls `getTrustedSystemAccessToken` with the shopper's `login_id`, which issues a new channel-scoped token server-side without prompting the customer. A registered shopper stays signed in transparently. A guest session does not carry over — guest tokens and baskets are site-scoped. **TSOB rate limit:** SLAS returns HTTP 409 if multiple TSOB calls are made for the same shopper within a 3-second window — the SSR layer must not fire duplicate TSOB calls on rapid storefront switches (debounce or dedupe at the MRT layer).
64	- **Baskets do not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency. Switching storefront starts a fresh basket; carrying one across a currency boundary would produce wrong prices.
65	- **Checkout handoff is a separate boundary.** When handing off to Global-e, the SLAS session does not extend into Global-e's hosted checkout.
66	
67	## 4. Data exchanged
68	
69	| Resource                           | Verbs                    | Notes                                                                                                                                           |
70	| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
71	| `/checkout/shopper-login/oauth2/*` | GET, POST                | SLAS authentication and token lifecycle                                                                                                         |
72	| `/product/shopper-products/v1/*`   | GET                      | Product details, master/variant resolution                                                                                                      |
73	| `/search/shopper-search/v1/*`      | GET                      | Catalogue search, faceting, sort, suggestions                                                                                                   |
74	| `/checkout/shopper-baskets/v2/*`   | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Basket lifecycle, line items, shipments, payment instruments                                                                                    |
75	| `/checkout/shopper-orders/v1/*`    | POST, GET                | Order placement and lookup (SFCC-owned checkouts only)                                                                                          |
76	| `/customer/shopper-customers/v1/*` | GET, POST, PATCH         | Profile, addresses, saved-payment references                                                                                                    |
77	| `/pricing/shopper-promotions/v1/*` | GET                      | Active promotions, coupon validation                                                                                                            |
78	| Einstein recommendations endpoints | GET                      | Personalised recommendations slot. Consent-gated (Didomi purpose TBC) — falls back to a static SFCC merchandising group if consent is not given |
79	
80	Every request carries the site ID, organisation ID, locale, currency, and SLAS bearer token. PII travels over TLS only. PCI scope is Adyen's — SFCC holds token references only.
81	
82	## 5. reCAPTCHA on register and login (CRM-008)
83	
84	- The storefront loads the reCAPTCHA v3 script on register and login forms only — not on any other page — and only after the customer first touches the form, so the script never blocks first paint.
85	- On submit, the reCAPTCHA token is sent alongside the form data to the MRT layer. The MRT layer verifies the token against Google's `siteverify` endpoint (using the secret key held as the `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` MRT environment variable) before forwarding the request to SCAPI. The secret key never reaches the browser.
86	- The site key is set per environment as `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (MRT environment variable, public). The secret key is held as `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (MRT environment variable, server-only).
87	- reCAPTCHA loads on form interaction regardless of consent. **Exception: EU and UK** — in those regions it only loads after Didomi consent, which means a visitor who declines gets no bot protection there.
88	
89	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
90	
91	- **HTTP/2** to a single SCAPI host; `<link rel="preconnect">` emitted in the document head.
92	- **TanStack Query** dedupes in-flight requests. Working defaults: stale time 60 s for catalogue, 30 s for promotions, 0 s for basket (always fresh).
93	- **SFCC edge cache** for anonymous catalogue traffic; cache keys include site, locale, currency, and customer group.
94	- **Parallel calls on PDP.** Product, recommendations, and promotions are fetched in parallel — no waterfall.
95	- **SSR fetches only critical data.** Recommendations and reviews load client-side after hydration.
96	- **Field projection.** SCAPI `fields=` parameters are used where supported to reduce payload size.
97	
98	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
99	
100	SFCC site IDs and Business Manager locale IDs verified against bkzk-002 Business Manager (2026-06-13):
101	
102	| SFCC Site ID               | BM Locale ID                                  | URL prefix                                 | Currency               | Checkout owner              |
103	| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------- | --------------------------- |
104	| `ZimmermannAU`             | `en`                                          | `/` (root, x-default hreflang)             | AUD                    | SFCC                        |
105	| `ZimmermannUS`             | `en-US`                                       | `/us/`                                     | USD                    | SFCC (US domestic)          |
106	| `ZimmermannUSIntl` _(TBC)_ | `en-US` _(TBC)_                               | `/en-ca/`                                  | USD                    | Global-e (US international) |
107	| `ZimmermannUK`             | `en-GB`                                       | `/uk/`                                     | GBP                    | SFCC                        |
108	| `ZimmermannEU`             | `en-GB` (EN), `fr` (FR), `it` (IT), `es` (ES) | `/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/` | EUR                    | SFCC                        |
109	| `ZimmermannEUIntl`         | `en-CH`                                       | `/en-ch/`                                  | EUR                    | Global-e                    |
110	| `ZimmermannHK`             | `en-HK`                                       | `/hk/`                                     | HKD (SFCC price books) | Global-e                    |
111	| `ZimmermannME`             | `en-AE`                                       | `/en-ae/`                                  | AED (SFCC price books) | Global-e                    |
112	
113	- The site ID is resolved from the URL prefix on every request (SSR and CSR).
114	- AU is geo-redirected for non-Oceania human visitors; verified search bots and social unfurlers are exempt via UA allowlist.
115	- Per-environment SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code remain outstanding — see §11 item 2.
116	
117	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
118	
119	| Failure                                       | Behaviour                                                                                                                                                                       |
120	| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
121	| SLAS unavailable                              | Storefront cannot mint a guest token and is non-operational. Show a maintenance message. P1 incident.                                                                           |
122	| SCAPI catalogue 5xx                           | TanStack Query retries three times with exponential backoff. On final failure, show the last cached payload if available; otherwise show an error state with a "Try again" CTA. |
123	| SCAPI basket 5xx during add-to-cart           | Inline error toast. The user's intent stays in client state so a retry resends the same request.                                                                                |
124	| Order placement 5xx after Adyen authorisation | Hard error — the order cannot fail silently. The customer sees an explicit error with a contact reference and ops is alerted.                                                   |
125	| Einstein recommendations 5xx                  | Hide the slot or fall back to a static merchandising group.                                                                                                                     |
126	| SLAS token refresh fails                      | Force re-login. The basket is preserved on the guest token until the customer completes checkout.                                                                               |
127	| TSOB 409 (rapid storefront switch)            | Retry after 3 seconds. Do not re-login the customer — the existing session is still valid on the origin channel.                                                                |
128	| reCAPTCHA fails to load or token rejected     | Block the register/login submit, show a "please retry" message, and offer a contact-support path after two failures.                                                            |
129	
130	## 9. Security and privacy
131	
132	- All traffic is TLS 1.2+ over HTTPS.
133	- SLAS private-client flow — the authorisation code exchange is proxied through MRT so the client secret never reaches the browser.
134	- Refresh tokens are held in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies — never in browser JavaScript.

# 01 — Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SCAPI) + reCAPTCHA

## 1. Purpose and scope

Salesforce Commerce Cloud B2C (SFCC) is the system of record for commerce data. The storefront calls SFCC directly from the browser via SCAPI for browsing, basket management, customer accounts, and order placement.

In scope:

- Authentication via Shopper Login & API Access Service (SLAS)
- Product catalogue, categories, search, recommendations
- Basket and cart
- Customer account (authentication record) and saved-payment token references
- Order placement for SFCC-owned checkouts (domestic markets)
- Gift cards — the storefront applies them via SCAPI; server-side redemption is outside the PWA boundary
- Google reCAPTCHA — browser-side script load on register/login forms; MRT-side token verification before SCAPI submission

At migration, only the customer's email and Omneo ID are stored in SFCC. Name, phone, addresses, and communication preferences come from Omneo at login (DMU-004). Order history comes from MuleSoft via the MRT proxy, not from SFCC (DMU-007).

Out of scope of this document:

- GiveX validate/redeem/refund, Avalara tax, Adyen back-office — all server-side, outside the PWA
- SFCC ↔ MuleSoft flows to NewStore, AP21, Omneo, Narvar
- Booxi appointment booking — MRT-mediated (PWA → MRT → Booxi), not a SFCC flow
- Business Manager configuration: promotions rules, content slots, Page Designer pages

## 2. Browser-side architecture

```
PWA (React, SSR + CSR)
        │
        │  @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react (TanStack Query under the hood)
        ▼
SLAS auth (guest or registered shopper) ──► Shopper context
        │                                       (site, currency, locale, customer)
        ▼
SCAPI: products, search, baskets, orders, customers, promotions, gift cards
        │
        ▼
SFCC realm
```

- **Single SDK.** `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` handles every SFCC call — SLAS token lifecycle, retry, and TanStack Query caching.
- **SSR and CSR.** Catalogue, PDP, PLP, content, and boutique pages are server-rendered for SEO and LCP. Cart, checkout, My Account, and order pages render an SSR shell and hydrate personalised data client-side after auth.
- **Managed Runtime.** The PWA Kit Node layer hosts the SSR pipeline and routes SLAS private-client calls through the server-side proxy.

## 3. Authentication and credentials

- **SLAS private-client flow** issues two token types: a guest access token (anonymous shopper, refreshed silently) and a registered shopper access token (issued after email/password login). Tokens are JWTs with a customer ID, unique shopper ID (USID), and refresh token.
- **Refresh tokens live in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies** set by the SSR layer. Browser JavaScript never sees the raw refresh token. On each refresh SLAS regenerates the token and voids the old one; the SSR layer rewrites the cookie in the same response.
- **Private client credentials.** The SLAS client secret is an MRT environment variable and never reaches the browser. The authorisation code exchange goes through the MRT private-client proxy (`privateClientProxyEndpoint`). The SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code stay in the bundle as public identifiers.
- **Social login.** Apple and Google via SLAS third-party identity-provider federation — confirmed in scope for launch; implementation design still open.
- **No Open Commerce API (OCAPI) credentials in the browser.** Any operation not yet covered by SCAPI is proxied through Managed Runtime with OCAPI credentials held server-side.

### Magento password migration (CFD-013)

Passwords were not migrated from Magento. All existing customers must reset at go-live. Failed sign-ins return a generic "invalid credentials" message (no email-existence leak) and the "forgot password" link is always visible.

### Cross-storefront session continuity

All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single domain and share one SFCC realm.

- **The refresh-token cookie is shared across storefronts.** Every storefront lives on the same domain, so the `httpOnly` cookie is sent on every path prefix. No cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.
- **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A token issued for `zimm-au` is not valid for `zimm-uk` — this is a hard SLAS platform constraint. On a storefront switch the SSR layer performs a fresh authorisation for the destination channel using the SLAS Trusted System on Behalf (TSOB) flow: it calls `getTrustedSystemAccessToken` with the shopper's `login_id`, which issues a new channel-scoped token server-side without prompting the customer. A registered shopper stays signed in transparently. A guest session does not carry over — guest tokens and baskets are site-scoped. **TSOB rate limit:** SLAS returns HTTP 409 if multiple TSOB calls are made for the same shopper within a 3-second window — the SSR layer must not fire duplicate TSOB calls on rapid storefront switches (debounce or dedupe at the MRT layer).
- **Baskets do not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency. Switching storefront starts a fresh basket; carrying one across a currency boundary would produce wrong prices.
- **Checkout handoff is a separate boundary.** When handing off to Global-e, the SLAS session does not extend into Global-e's hosted checkout.

## 4. Data exchanged

| Resource                           | Verbs                    | Notes                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/checkout/shopper-login/oauth2/*` | GET, POST                | SLAS authentication and token lifecycle                                                                                                         |
| `/product/shopper-products/v1/*`   | GET                      | Product details, master/variant resolution                                                                                                      |
| `/search/shopper-search/v1/*`      | GET                      | Catalogue search, faceting, sort, suggestions                                                                                                   |
| `/checkout/shopper-baskets/v2/*`   | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE | Basket lifecycle, line items, shipments, payment instruments                                                                                    |
| `/checkout/shopper-orders/v1/*`    | POST, GET                | Order placement and lookup (SFCC-owned checkouts only)                                                                                          |
| `/customer/shopper-customers/v1/*` | GET, POST, PATCH         | Profile, addresses, saved-payment references                                                                                                    |
| `/pricing/shopper-promotions/v1/*` | GET                      | Active promotions, coupon validation                                                                                                            |
| Einstein recommendations endpoints | GET                      | Personalised recommendations slot. Consent-gated (Didomi purpose TBC) — falls back to a static SFCC merchandising group if consent is not given |

Every request carries the site ID, organisation ID, locale, currency, and SLAS bearer token. PII travels over TLS only. PCI scope is Adyen's — SFCC holds token references only.

## 5. reCAPTCHA on register and login (CRM-008)

- The storefront loads the reCAPTCHA v3 script on register and login forms only — not on any other page — and only after the customer first touches the form, so the script never blocks first paint.
- On submit, the reCAPTCHA token is sent alongside the form data to the MRT layer. The MRT layer verifies the token against Google's `siteverify` endpoint (using the secret key held as the `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` MRT environment variable) before forwarding the request to SCAPI. The secret key never reaches the browser.
- The site key is set per environment as `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (MRT environment variable, public). The secret key is held as `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (MRT environment variable, server-only).
- reCAPTCHA loads on form interaction regardless of consent. **Exception: EU and UK** — in those regions it only loads after Didomi consent, which means a visitor who declines gets no bot protection there.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- **HTTP/2** to a single SCAPI host; `<link rel="preconnect">` emitted in the document head.
- **TanStack Query** dedupes in-flight requests. Working defaults: stale time 60 s for catalogue, 30 s for promotions, 0 s for basket (always fresh).
- **SFCC edge cache** for anonymous catalogue traffic; cache keys include site, locale, currency, and customer group.
- **Parallel calls on PDP.** Product, recommendations, and promotions are fetched in parallel — no waterfall.
- **SSR fetches only critical data.** Recommendations and reviews load client-side after hydration.
- **Field projection.** SCAPI `fields=` parameters are used where supported to reduce payload size.

## 7. Multi-region behaviour

SFCC site IDs and Business Manager locale IDs verified against bkzk-002 Business Manager (2026-06-13):

| SFCC Site ID               | BM Locale ID                                  | URL prefix                                 | Currency               | Checkout owner              |
| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `ZimmermannAU`             | `en`                                          | `/` (root, x-default hreflang)             | AUD                    | SFCC                        |
| `ZimmermannUS`             | `en-US`                                       | `/us/`                                     | USD                    | SFCC (US domestic)          |
| `ZimmermannUSIntl` _(TBC)_ | `en-US` _(TBC)_                               | `/en-ca/`                                  | USD                    | Global-e (US international) |
| `ZimmermannUK`             | `en-GB`                                       | `/uk/`                                     | GBP                    | SFCC                        |
| `ZimmermannEU`             | `en-GB` (EN), `fr` (FR), `it` (IT), `es` (ES) | `/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/` | EUR                    | SFCC                        |
| `ZimmermannEUIntl`         | `en-CH`                                       | `/en-ch/`                                  | EUR                    | Global-e                    |
| `ZimmermannHK`             | `en-HK`                                       | `/hk/`                                     | HKD (SFCC price books) | Global-e                    |
| `ZimmermannME`             | `en-AE`                                       | `/en-ae/`                                  | AED (SFCC price books) | Global-e                    |

- The site ID is resolved from the URL prefix on every request (SSR and CSR).
- AU is geo-redirected for non-Oceania human visitors; verified search bots and social unfurlers are exempt via UA allowlist.
- Per-environment SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code remain outstanding — see §11 item 2.

## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure                                       | Behaviour                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| SLAS unavailable                              | Storefront cannot mint a guest token and is non-operational. Show a maintenance message. P1 incident.                                                                           |
| SCAPI catalogue 5xx                           | TanStack Query retries three times with exponential backoff. On final failure, show the last cached payload if available; otherwise show an error state with a "Try again" CTA. |
| SCAPI basket 5xx during add-to-cart           | Inline error toast. The user's intent stays in client state so a retry resends the same request.                                                                                |
| Order placement 5xx after Adyen authorisation | Hard error — the order cannot fail silently. The customer sees an explicit error with a contact reference and ops is alerted.                                                   |
| Einstein recommendations 5xx                  | Hide the slot or fall back to a static merchandising group.                                                                                                                     |
| SLAS token refresh fails                      | Force re-login. The basket is preserved on the guest token until the customer completes checkout.                                                                               |
| TSOB 409 (rapid storefront switch)            | Retry after 3 seconds. Do not re-login the customer — the existing session is still valid on the origin channel.                                                                |
| reCAPTCHA fails to load or token rejected     | Block the register/login submit, show a "please retry" message, and offer a contact-support path after two failures.                                                            |

## 9. Security and privacy

- All traffic is TLS 1.2+ over HTTPS.
- SLAS private-client flow — the authorisation code exchange is proxied through MRT so the client secret never reaches the browser.
- Refresh tokens are held in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies — never in browser JavaScript.
- PCI scope is Adyen's — the browser sends payment data directly to Adyen. SFCC holds token references only.

## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **Login MFA scope.** Confirm whether multi-factor authentication on login is in scope for launch or post-launch. If in scope, the SLAS configuration and the PWA login flow need additional design.

2. **`sfPayments.metadataUrl` hostname.** The `sfcc-payments` undici connection pool (TSD §12.1) holds `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl`'s origin in a pool separate from `sfcc-scapi` (`{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`). That separation only provides blast-radius isolation if the two hosts are different origins. If `sfPayments.metadataUrl` resolves to the same SCAPI host, the pools should be merged.

1	# 03 — MuleSoft (PWA-direct reads via MRT proxy)
2	
3	## 1. Purpose and scope
4	
5	MuleSoft is the integration middleware that sits between SFCC and Zimmermann's back-office systems (NewStore OMS, AP21, Omneo, Narvar). The vast majority of MuleSoft traffic is server-to-server from SFCC and is out of scope here. This document covers the **separate, direct path** in which the PWA's Managed Runtime Node layer calls MuleSoft directly via `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...` for a small set of read operations where SFCC adds no value to the round-trip.
6	
7	Operations in scope of this document (PWA → MRT → MuleSoft, with SFCC outside the read path):
8	
9	- Order history list (CRM-056 / CRM-057, RRC-013) — the 50 most recent orders, online and in-store
10	- Order detail (CRM-071 / CRM-072)
11	- Account dashboard "recent orders" summary (CRM-029, OM-017, OM-035)
12	- Returns data for the My Account returns view (CRM-088)
13	- Real-time stock availability:
14	  - Find in Boutique flyout and BOPIS boutique selection screen (CFD-043, CAI-038)
15	  - Collect in Boutique store + size validation (CAI-043)
16	  - Cart → checkout entry stock check (CAI-034 — this MuleSoft flow does not yet exist; the storefront falls back to the inventory feed until it is built)
17	- GiveX balance check (GC-037, GC-053) — MRT proxies an HTTPS request to MuleSoft, which owns the GiveX TCP connection and credentials
18	
19	Operations out of scope (server-to-server, outside the PWA layer):
20	
21	- SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore order creation and fulfilment writes
22	- SFCC ↔ MuleSoft ↔ Omneo customer / loyalty / address sync
23	- SFCC → MuleSoft → AP21 retail rewards balance lookup
24	- Product and pricing master feed AP21 → MuleSoft → SFCC (catalogue and pricebooks)
25	- The daily and 15-minute inventory feeds NewStore → MuleSoft → SFCC (CAI-019, CAI-020)
26	- Adyen fraud webhooks via MuleSoft (PAY-046)
27	- GiveX validate / redeem / refund (server-side via SCAPI/SFCC → NewStore adaptor → MuleSoft → GiveX)
28	- GiveX gift-card **issuance** at purchase (SCAPI/SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore → GiveX)
29	
30	## 2. PWA-layer architecture
31	
32	The flow below reflects the confirmed design from the MuleSoft integration PDFs (Jun 2025). MRT authenticates to MuleSoft using platform credentials (`client_id` + `client_secret`). The `customer_id` is passed as a plain UUID query parameter; MuleSoft does not verify shopper identity at the transport layer.
33	
34	```
35	Browser (My Account, cart, BOPIS flyout, etc.)
36	        │  Authenticated customer — customer_id known from SFCC session
37	        ▼
38	PWA fetches /mobify/proxy/mulesoft/<endpoint>
39	        │
40	        ▼
41	MRT Node layer:
42	   1. Reads customer_id from the authenticated SFCC session
43	   2. Appends client_id + client_secret as HTTP request headers (MRT environment variables)
44	   3. Forwards to https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api[-{env}]/<path>
45	      (env suffix: `-dev` for Dev, `-qa` for QA; no suffix for Prod — per vendor docs)
46	      with customer_id as a query parameter
47	        │
48	        ▼
49	MuleSoft (Magento Experience API):
50	   • Verifies channel auth via client_id + client_secret
51	   • Does NOT verify shopper identity at the transport layer
52	   • Routes internally to the Order Transactions Sync Process API → NewStore
53	        │
54	        ▼
55	NewStore response → MuleSoft → MRT → Browser (typed JSON, only the fields needed)
56	```
57	
58	- The browser never carries MuleSoft credentials. `client_id` and `client_secret` are held as MRT environment variables and are never exposed to the browser bundle.
59	- `customer_id` is a UUID string. MRT reads it from the authenticated SFCC session (step 1 above) — never from browser-supplied input. This prevents a browser from retrieving another customer's data by substituting a different UUID.
60	
61	## 3. Endpoint inventory
62	
63	Endpoints marked ✅ have confirmed paths and response schemas from the MuleSoft technical design documents. Endpoints marked ⏳ are working assumptions pending the formal OpenAPI specification (open item 1 in §9).
64	
65	| Endpoint | Status | Used by | Backed by | Requirement |
66	|---|---|---|---|---|
67	| `GET /api/orders?customer_id={…}&offset={…}&count={…}` | ✅ | Order history list (My Account) | NewStore | CRM-056, CRM-057, OM-035, RRC-013 |
68	| `GET /api/orders/{order_id}?id_type=internal` | ✅ | Order detail page | NewStore | CRM-071, CRM-072 |
69	| `GET /api/returns?customer_id={…}&offset={…}&count={…}` | ✅ | My Account returns view | NewStore Returns API | CRM-088, RRC-007 |
70	| `POST /api/find-in-store` body: `{ProductId, CountryCode}` | ✅ | Find in Boutique flyout + BOPIS screen | NewStore | CFD-043, CAI-038 |
71	| Orders list with `count=3` — confirm path with integration team | ⏳ | Account dashboard summary | NewStore | CRM-029 |
72	| GiveX balance check — path TBC; flows PWA → MRT → MuleSoft → GiveX (MuleSoft owns the GiveX TCP socket pool) | ⏳ | Gift card balance in My Account and at checkout | GiveX via MuleSoft | GC-037, GC-053 |
73	| Collect in Boutique validation — path TBC | ⏳ | Collect in Boutique store + size validation | NewStore | CAI-043 |
74	| Cart → checkout entry stock check — MuleSoft flow not yet built | ⏳ | Cart → checkout entry | NewStore | CAI-034 |
75	
76	The full OpenAPI specification is open item 1 in §9.
77	
78	## 4. Authentication and credentials
79	
80	| Credential | Where used | Sensitivity |
81	|---|---|---|
82	| `client_id` | MRT environment variable; sent on every request to MuleSoft as an HTTP request header (never as a URL query parameter) | Secret — never reaches the browser |
83	| `client_secret` | MRT environment variable; sent on every request to MuleSoft as an HTTP request header (never as a URL query parameter) | Secret — never reaches the browser |
84	| `customer_id` (UUID) | Plain query parameter on orders / returns calls; read from the SFCC session server-side | Not a secret — MRT enforces it matches the authenticated session |
85	
86	One `client_id` / `client_secret` pair per environment. Credential rotation is owned by the integration team.
87	
88	## 5. Data exchanged
89	
90	| Direction | Data | Notes |
91	|---|---|---|
92	| Browser → MRT | Authenticated customer session (customer_id extracted server-side); endpoint path; small query/body payload where applicable | The browser never sees MuleSoft credentials. |
93	| MRT → MuleSoft | `client_id` + `client_secret` (channel auth); `customer_id` as a query parameter; endpoint payload | `client_id`/`client_secret` authorise the channel. MuleSoft does not verify shopper identity at the transport layer. |
94	| MuleSoft → MRT → Browser | Typed JSON — order summary, order detail, boutique stock list, returns list | MRT projects only the fields the UI consumes to keep payload small. |
95	
96	No PII flows back to the browser beyond what the customer already owns (their own order data, their own returns). Boutique stock responses contain no PII.
97	
98	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
99	
100	- All MuleSoft reads are made only when the relevant route or interaction triggers them. The order-history list does not preload on home; the boutique inventory call only fires when the Find in Boutique flyout opens (CAI-038).
101	- The MuleSoft vendor response time target (per the received PDFs) is < 2.5 s. The PWA's own soft-failure threshold of 2 s (see §7) is intentionally stricter.
102	- Working performance budget (working assumption — pending SLA confirmation with the integration team): p95 under 800 ms for order list and order detail; under 500 ms for boutique inventory checks.
103	- TanStack Query caches order list and order detail responses on the client; stale data is acceptable for the dashboard summary and order list but never for cart → checkout entry stock checks, which always re-fetch.
104	- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the MuleSoft host is emitted from the My Account entry routes once the customer is authenticated.
105	
106	## 7. Failure modes and graceful degradation
107	
108	| Failure | Behaviour |
109	|---|---|
110	| MuleSoft rejects channel auth (invalid `client_id`/`client_secret`) | Return 401 to the browser. This indicates a misconfigured or rotated credential — requires an ops fix, not a user retry. Surface a generic error UI. |
111	| MuleSoft 5xx on order list | Order history view shows an explicit retry UI. The contract is "explicit retry, never partial data". |
112	| MuleSoft 5xx on cart → checkout entry stock check (CAI-034) | Block checkout entry with a clear error. Do not silently progress; a stale stock decision risks an oversell. |
113	| MuleSoft 5xx on Find in Boutique inventory (CFD-043) | Show "Stock information temporarily unavailable" inside the flyout and a retry CTA. Do not fall back to cached data — boutique stock is real-time by design. |
114	| MuleSoft 5xx on Collect in Boutique validation (CAI-043) | Reject the boutique selection with an error; the shopper can pick a different store or method. |
115	| MuleSoft timeout above 2 seconds | Treated as a soft failure. UI degrades gracefully per the rows above. |
116	| NewStore upstream of MuleSoft is down | Surfaced to the storefront as a MuleSoft 5xx. Same handling. |
117	
118	## 8. Security and privacy
119	
120	- `client_id` and `client_secret` are held as MRT environment variables and never appear in browser JavaScript, request URLs, or client-accessible logs.
121	- All MRT → MuleSoft traffic is over TLS 1.2+.
122	- `customer_id` is a plain UUID query parameter passed to MuleSoft. MuleSoft does not verify shopper identity at the transport layer — MuleSoft trusts the channel. Impersonation is prevented at the MRT layer: MRT reads `customer_id` from the authenticated SFCC session only, never from browser-supplied input.
123	- No PII is logged at the MRT layer beyond a request ID and the endpoint name.
124	
125	## 9. Open items requiring client confirmation
126	
127	1. **MuleSoft OpenAPI specification.** MuleSoft to publish a versioned OpenAPI document covering every endpoint the storefront calls (order history and detail, returns, gift-card balance check, and any other MuleSoft-fronted endpoint in scope), including request and response schemas, error codes, and pagination contracts. The PDFs received (Jun 2025) provide sample schemas sufficient for initial implementation, but a formal versioned spec is still needed.
128	2. **Per-environment MuleSoft credentials.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: `client_id`, `client_secret`, and MuleSoft host. Prod URLs for orders and returns are not yet provisioned (blank in the received PDFs). A staging Find In Store URL has been received (`https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api/api/find-in-store`); the production host is not yet confirmed.
129	3. **Response payload contracts for order detail and returns — mostly resolved.** Full sample schemas for order list, order detail, and returns were extracted from the Magento Experience Integration and Customer Order Transactions Sync PDFs (v3.0 / v2.0, Jun 2025) and are sufficient for initial implementation. Minor residual points to confirm with Tryzens: `channel.type` values for online orders (sample data only shows in-store); whether the returns endpoint supports `offset`/`count` pagination; the `shop.id` inconsistency between list (`"storefront-catalog-eu"`) and detail (`"ZIMMERMANN_LONDON_STORE"`) responses; the full set of `psp` values for online payment methods (sample shows `"cash"` and `"store_credit"` only).
130

- `customer_id` is a UUID string. MRT reads it from the authenticated SFCC session (step 1 above) — never from browser-supplied input. This prevents a browser from retrieving another customer's data by substituting a different UUID.

## 3. Endpoint inventory

Endpoints marked ✅ have confirmed paths and response schemas from the MuleSoft technical design documents. Endpoints marked ⏳ are working assumptions pending the formal OpenAPI specification (open item 1 in §9).

| Endpoint | Status | Used by | Backed by | Requirement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/orders?customer_id={…}&offset={…}&count={…}` | ✅ | Order history list (My Account) | NewStore | CRM-056, CRM-057, OM-035, RRC-013 |
| `GET /api/orders/{order_id}?id_type=internal` | ✅ | Order detail page | NewStore | CRM-071, CRM-072 |
| `GET /api/returns?customer_id={…}&offset={…}&count={…}` | ✅ | My Account returns view | NewStore Returns API | CRM-088, RRC-007 |
| `POST /api/find-in-store` body: `{ProductId, CountryCode}` | ✅ | Find in Boutique flyout + BOPIS screen | NewStore | CFD-043, CAI-038 |
| Orders list with `count=3` — confirm path with integration team | ⏳ | Account dashboard summary | NewStore | CRM-029 |
| GiveX balance check — path TBC; flows PWA → MRT → MuleSoft → GiveX (MuleSoft owns the GiveX TCP socket pool) | ⏳ | Gift card balance in My Account and at checkout | GiveX via MuleSoft | GC-037, GC-053 |
| Collect in Boutique validation — path TBC | ⏳ | Collect in Boutique store + size validation | NewStore | CAI-043 |
| Cart → checkout entry stock check — MuleSoft flow not yet built | ⏳ | Cart → checkout entry | NewStore | CAI-034 |

The full OpenAPI specification is open item 1 in §9.

## 4. Authentication and credentials

| Credential | Where used | Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| `client_id` | MRT environment variable; sent on every request to MuleSoft as an HTTP request header (never as a URL query parameter) | Secret — never reaches the browser |
| `client_secret` | MRT environment variable; sent on every request to MuleSoft as an HTTP request header (never as a URL query parameter) | Secret — never reaches the browser |
| `customer_id` (UUID) | Plain query parameter on orders / returns calls; read from the SFCC session server-side | Not a secret — MRT enforces it matches the authenticated session |

One `client_id` / `client_secret` pair per environment. Credential rotation is owned by the integration team.

## 5. Data exchanged

| Direction | Data | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Browser → MRT | Authenticated customer session (customer_id extracted server-side); endpoint path; small query/body payload where applicable | The browser never sees MuleSoft credentials. |
| MRT → MuleSoft | `client_id` + `client_secret` (channel auth); `customer_id` as a query parameter; endpoint payload | `client_id`/`client_secret` authorise the channel. MuleSoft does not verify shopper identity at the transport layer. |
| MuleSoft → MRT → Browser | Typed JSON — order summary, order detail, boutique stock list, returns list | MRT projects only the fields the UI consumes to keep payload small. |

No PII flows back to the browser beyond what the customer already owns (their own order data, their own returns). Boutique stock responses contain no PII.

## 6. Performance and loading strategy

- All MuleSoft reads are made only when the relevant route or interaction triggers them. The order-history list does not preload on home; the boutique inventory call only fires when the Find in Boutique flyout opens (CAI-038).
- The MuleSoft vendor response time target (per the received PDFs) is < 2.5 s. The PWA's own soft-failure threshold of 2 s (see §7) is intentionally stricter.
- Working performance budget (working assumption — pending SLA confirmation with the integration team): p95 under 800 ms for order list and order detail; under 500 ms for boutique inventory checks.
- TanStack Query caches order list and order detail responses on the client; stale data is acceptable for the dashboard summary and order list but never for cart → checkout entry stock checks, which always re-fetch.
- `<link rel="preconnect">` to the MuleSoft host is emitted from the My Account entry routes once the customer is authenticated.

## 7. Failure modes and graceful degradation

| Failure | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| MuleSoft rejects channel auth (invalid `client_id`/`client_secret`) | Return 401 to the browser. This indicates a misconfigured or rotated credential — requires an ops fix, not a user retry. Surface a generic error UI. |
| MuleSoft 5xx on order list | Order history view shows an explicit retry UI. The contract is "explicit retry, never partial data". |
| MuleSoft 5xx on cart → checkout entry stock check (CAI-034) | Block checkout entry with a clear error. Do not silently progress; a stale stock decision risks an oversell. |
| MuleSoft 5xx on Find in Boutique inventory (CFD-043) | Show "Stock information temporarily unavailable" inside the flyout and a retry CTA. Do not fall back to cached data — boutique stock is real-time by design. |
| MuleSoft 5xx on Collect in Boutique validation (CAI-043) | Reject the boutique selection with an error; the shopper can pick a different store or method. |
| MuleSoft timeout above 2 seconds | Treated as a soft failure. UI degrades gracefully per the rows above. |
| NewStore upstream of MuleSoft is down | Surfaced to the storefront as a MuleSoft 5xx. Same handling. |

## 8. Security and privacy

- `client_id` and `client_secret` are held as MRT environment variables and never appear in browser JavaScript, request URLs, or client-accessible logs.
- All MRT → MuleSoft traffic is over TLS 1.2+.
- `customer_id` is a plain UUID query parameter passed to MuleSoft. MuleSoft does not verify shopper identity at the transport layer — MuleSoft trusts the channel. Impersonation is prevented at the MRT layer: MRT reads `customer_id` from the authenticated SFCC session only, never from browser-supplied input.
- No PII is logged at the MRT layer beyond a request ID and the endpoint name.

## 9. Open items requiring client confirmation

1. **MuleSoft OpenAPI specification.** MuleSoft to publish a versioned OpenAPI document covering every endpoint the storefront calls (order history and detail, returns, gift-card balance check, and any other MuleSoft-fronted endpoint in scope), including request and response schemas, error codes, and pagination contracts. The PDFs received (Jun 2025) provide sample schemas sufficient for initial implementation, but a formal versioned spec is still needed.
2. **Per-environment MuleSoft credentials.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: `client_id`, `client_secret`, and MuleSoft host. Prod URLs for orders and returns are not yet provisioned (blank in the received PDFs). A staging Find In Store URL has been received (`https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api/api/find-in-store`); the production host is not yet confirmed.
3. **Response payload contracts for order detail and returns — mostly resolved.** Full sample schemas for order list, order detail, and returns were extracted from the Magento Experience Integration and Customer Order Transactions Sync PDFs (v3.0 / v2.0, Jun 2025) and are sufficient for initial implementation. Minor residual points to confirm with Tryzens: `channel.type` values for online orders (sample data only shows in-store); whether the returns endpoint supports `offset`/`count` pagination; the `shop.id` inconsistency between list (`"storefront-catalog-eu"`) and detail (`"ZIMMERMANN_LONDON_STORE"`) responses; the full set of `psp` values for online payment methods (sample shows `"cash"` and `"store_credit"` only).

1. Purpose & Scope
------------------

This TSD describes the technical foundation for the Zimmermann production storefront at <http://www.zimmermann.com> — a luxury Australian fashion brand running on Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) PWA Kit.

**In scope:**

* Stack and build pipeline
* The customisation model on top of `@salesforce/retail-react-app`
* Multi-site / multi-locale routing across 8 storefronts in 6 regions
* Integration map (SFCC, MuleSoft, Contentful, Global-e, Didomi, Adyen, Omneo, Narvar, GiveX, Google Places)
* SSR + SEO foundation (DMU-030, hreflang, sitemaps, structured data)
* Performance budgets, accessibility, consent gating, GDPR
* Testing strategy and CI/CD topology
* Open decisions requiring client input before build

**Out of scope:** per-feature functional design; detailed per-vendor integration design

---

2. Solution Overview
--------------------

A single PWA Kit codebase serves 8 logical SFCC sites, each with its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, payment methods, and consent defaults. International checkout is owned by Global-e; domestic checkout is owned by SFCC. All order-creation, fulfilment write, and CRM sync traffic from SFCC routes through **MuleSoft** as the middleware boundary — SFCC does not call NewStore, AP21, Omneo, or Narvar directly. In addition, the PWA's MRT Node layer calls MuleSoft directly (via `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...`) for read operations: order history, order details, boutique stock checks (Find in Boutique, Collect in Boutique), GiveX balance check, and real-time stock availability. These reads bypass SFCC entirely.

The PWA itself also talks to a handful of services without going through SFCC. Contentful and Didomi are browser-direct. Google Maps (Places API), GiveX balance check (proxied through MuleSoft — see §2 GiveX note), and select MuleSoft operations are called from the PWA's MRT Node layer via proxy, with API credentials held server-side as MRT environment variables.

Legend / boundaries:

* **PWA → Contentful, Vimeo, Didomi, GTM (via Addingwell), Optimizely Web, Crazy Egg, Inside Chat, Narvar Promise, Adyen Drop-In, Measmerize:** browser-direct; no SFCC involvement. GTM, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Inside Chat, and Narvar Promise load post-Didomi-consent only.

* **SFCC → MuleSoft → NewStore / AP21 / Omneo / Narvar:** write and sync flows initiated by SFCC.
* **AP21 → MuleSoft → SFCC (inbound):** product and pricing master feed into the SFCC catalogue and pricebooks.
* **Omneo iFrame (My Account):** also surfaced as a browser-direct iFrame in My Account (CRM-176); all other Omneo traffic via MuleSoft.
