3. Frontend Stack
-----------------

### 3.1 Bundled by PWA Kit

| Layer | Library | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Base framework | PWA Kit on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 | Current baseline |
| UI framework | React 18 + Chakra UI | Component library + theme tokens |
| Routing | React Router v6 |  |
| Server / async state | TanStack Query via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` | All SFCC data fetching |
| i18n | react-intl | Translations under `translations/` |
| Build / dev | Webpack 5 via `pwa-kit-dev` |  |

### 3.2 Project additions

| Layer | Library | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Type safety | TypeScript strict mode | All custom code is `.ts` / `.tsx` |
| Component explorer | Storybook 8 + `@storybook/addon-a11y` | `play` functions for interaction tests |
| Unit testing | Vitest (+ `vitest-axe`) | Project-level test runner |
| E2E | Playwright (+ `axe-playwright`) | Multi-region fixtures from day one |
| Forms | react-hook-form + zod | Introduced when checkout / account work begins |
| Global UI state | Zustand | Per-request store in SSR |

---

4. Customisation Model
----------------------

This project uses the Salesforce PWA Kit's *template extensibility* model. `@salesforce/retail-react-app` is consumed as an unmodified npm dependency, not a forked copy of the repository.

All customisations live in an `overrides/` directory that mirrors the structure of the underlying `@salesforce/retail-react-app` package. The base package is consumed unmodified — overrides take precedence at resolution time. This keeps the project upgradeable: pulling a new Salesforce baseline is a dependency bump plus a targeted reconciliation of overridden files, not a full re-application of patches.

**Working principle:** stay as close to base PWA Kit behaviour as possible. Visual changes (Chakra props, theme tokens, SCSS where Chakra is insufficient) are expected. Structural changes (data flow, routing, or layout deviations from the base template) are taken deliberately and reviewed against the upgrade impact before being merged.

**Brand-new components** (with no base equivalent) will also live in the `overrides/` folder.

### 4.1 Environment Configuration

All secrets and per-tier identifiers are injected as **Managed Runtime environment variables**. Unless public identifiers, they must never be committed to source control or exposed in client-side bundles. The canonical list of every variable the storefront expects is maintained in the project's environment-variable template, grouped by integration with inline comments — that template is the single source of truth. The table below shows the groups so each credential's boundary is clear.

| Group | Purpose | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `COMMERCE_API_*`, `EINSTEIN_API_SITE_ID` | SFCC SCAPI / SLAS client config | Browser-direct (public client ID) + MRT-mediated (token refresh) |
| `GOOGLE_CLOUD_API_KEY` | Google Maps Places API (address autocomplete) | MRT-mediated — key never reaches the browser |
| `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID`, `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID`, `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` | Contentful Delivery API (published content) | Browser + SSR. CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment; safe in bundle but held as an MRT env var so rotation is centralised |
| `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN`, `CONTENTFUL_HOST` | Contentful Preview API (drafts, editor sessions) | MRT-mediated — proxied server-side; never reaches the browser |
| `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Contentful Management API (schema sync) | **Local / CI only** — never deployed to MRT |
| `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Shared secret for the Contentful → MRT cache-purge webhook (HMAC verification) | MRT-mediated |
| `MULESOFT_BASE_URL`, `MULESOFT_CLIENT_ID`, `MULESOFT_CLIENT_SECRET` | PWA → MuleSoft direct calls (`/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...`): order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock, GiveX balance | MRT-mediated — credentials never reach the browser |
| `ADYEN_CLIENT_KEY`, `ADYEN_ENVIRONMENT` | Adyen Drop-In / Components SDK at checkout (tokenisation, 3DS2 inline). Server-side `/payments` calls and HMAC live in SFCC BM | Browser-direct — client key is public by design (PAY-021) |

| `NARVAR_ACCOUNT_ID` | Narvar Promise (formerly CONVERT) EDD widget at checkout (domestic only) | Browser-direct — public ID |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` | reCAPTCHA v3 site key (registration / login forms) | Browser-direct — public site key only |
| `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | reCAPTCHA v3 secret key — used by the MRT layer to verify tokens against Google's `siteverify` endpoint; never reaches the browser | MRT-mediated |
| `GLOBALE_*` | Global-e merchant ID, environment, script host, supported countries, server-side API key | Browser-direct (script host, merchant ID) + MRT-mediated (API key, if used) — final shape pending PRC-34..43 sign-off |
| `DIDOMI_API_KEY` | Didomi Notice/Consent ID | Browser-direct — public ID, safe in bundle |
| `GTM_CONTAINER_ID`, `GTM_SERVER_URL` | GTM container and Addingwell first-party tagging-server hostname (`<https://ruffles.zimmermann.com`).> The loader uses both: `${GTM_SERVER_URL}/gtm.js?id=${GTM_CONTAINER_ID}` | Browser-direct — both public, safe in bundle. One pair per environment |
| `SENTRY_DSN`, `NEW_RELIC_LICENSE_KEY`, `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` | Observability | MRT-mediated (license keys held server-side); `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` (one of `local`, `dev`, `sit`, `stage`, `uat`, `prod`) is the per-tier tag emitted to Sentry / New Relic / GTM |
| `MARKETING_CLOUD_*`, `COMMERCE_AGENT_SETTINGS`, `OTP_TOKEN_LENGTH` | PWA Kit base-template defaults referenced by the base runtime configuration | Likely removable once email/auth wiring is finalised (Zimmermann uses Emarsys via Omneo, not Marketing Cloud) |

**Security policy:**

* Real values live only in local, untracked environment files — one shared file (`.env.shared`, tier-independent) plus one per deployment tier (`.env.<tier>` for dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod), managed via `npm run env` (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`). Only a template — variable names tagged `# scope:shared|tier|personal|auto` on their own comment line, no secret values — is committed to source control as `.env.sample`. Two guardrails enforce this: a pre-commit hook that blocks commit if `.env.sample` contains a secret-shaped non-empty value, and a Claude Code rule that instructs the AI assistant never to write real secret values into `.env.sample`.
* Public identifiers (e.g. the GTM container ID, Didomi notice ID, SFCC SLAS client ID) may carry placeholder values in the committed template.
* Secrets (tokens, license keys, HMAC secrets, server-side API keys) appear in the committed template as the variable name only, with an empty value.
* Non-personal shared/tier values can be centrally published and pulled via this repo's GitHub Environments (`shared` + one per deployment tier under Settings > Environments), stored as GitHub Environment Variables — write access requires repo Admin (`@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`), read access is repo-collaborator-wide. This is a deliberate, documented exception to using GitHub Secrets (which cannot be read back via API once set) — see `.env.sample`'s header for the full rationale. Genuinely personal credentials (`scope:personal` — your own Jira/Confluence token, your own Contentful CMA token) are always excluded from this and never centralized.
* MRT variables are managed per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod) in the Managed Runtime console and rotated independently of the codebase.

---

5. Multi-Site, Multi-Locale Architecture
----------------------------------------

### 5.1 Storefronts

**8 independent SFCC sites across 6 regions**, each with its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, and payment methods. 11 active locales total. US/EU domestic and international are configured as separate SFCC sites (REG-006).

| Locale | URL prefix | Currency | Checkout owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AU + Oceania | `/` (x-default hreflang) | AUD | SFCC (REG-003) |
| UK | `/uk/` | GBP | SFCC (REG-004) |
| US domestic | `/us/` | USD | SFCC (REG-005) |
| US international | `/en-ca/` | USD | Global-e (REG-005) |
| EU domestic — EN / FR / IT / ES | `/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/` | EUR | SFCC (REG-006 dom) |
| EU international | `/en-ch/` | EUR | Global-e (REG-006 intl) |
| HK | `/hk/` | HKD (Global-e display) | Global-e (REG-007) |
| ME | `/en-ae/` | AED (Global-e display) | Global-e (REG-008) |

Rest-of-world traffic routes via `/en-ch/` and `/en-ca/` (DMU-013). AU is configured at the root with no locale prefix and serves as the x-default hreflang target (DMU-016).

### 5.2 Entry routing

* **IP geolocation** selects the site on first visit (REG-013).
* **AU is gated** to Oceania IPs only (REG-009) but remains the x-default hreflang target, so gating runs in the application layer rather than at the network. Non-Oceania human visitors are redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; verified search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt; UA ambiguity fails open (false positives have no SEO cost; missing a real crawler does).
* **Cross-region entry handling for all other storefronts** — first-visit mismatch-detection slide-out, the country/language selector, and the EU language-mismatch modal — is functional design (REG-014–035), out of scope for this TSD.

### 5.3 Single source of truth for country / locale

Country, locale, currency, shipping country, Global-e flag, and boutique-region data live in a single front-end configuration module. When a market is added, that module and the SFCC site configuration are updated together.

### 5.4 Per-storefront concerns that must not bleed

* **Consent defaults (REG-054):** per-storefront Didomi defaults are site-scoped config that must not bleed across storefronts; the values themselves are specified under REG-054.
* **Tax model:** SFCC native tax tables (AU GST, UK VAT); Avalara for US domestic, NZ, New Caledonia, and EU domestic (EU domestic added 2026-06-19); Global-e handles tax for international checkout paths.
* **Marketing opt-in default (REG-057):** site-scoped per storefront; must not bleed — value specified under REG-057.
* **Payment methods:** per-storefront Adyen configuration. Apple Pay, Google Pay, and Klarna are post-launch.

### 5.5 Session and basket scope across storefronts

All eight storefronts are path-prefixed on a single first-party domain and run on a single SFCC realm with shared customer data. This determines how a shopper's session behaves when they cross storefronts (via the country / language selector or the mismatch slide-out):

* **Session cookie is shared.** The `httpOnly` SLAS refresh-token cookie set by the SSR layer is first-party to the one domain, so it is presented on requests to any storefront prefix — no cross-domain SSO bridge is needed.
* **Tokens are channel-scoped.** A SLAS token carries the site it was issued for, so the SSR layer re-initialises the SLAS context for the destination storefront. Because the customer record is shared across the realm, a registered shopper is silently re-recognised without re-entering credentials; a guest session is site-scoped and does not carry over.
* **Basket does not transfer — by design.** Baskets are site-scoped and priced in the storefront's own currency against its own pricebook, so a shopper switching storefront starts a fresh basket. Carrying a basket across a currency / pricebook boundary would produce incorrect pricing.
* **Checkout handoff is separate.** When an international storefront hands off to Global-e, the SLAS session does not extend into the Global-e hosted checkout — Global-e owns that session in full.

6. Checkout Ownership Branching
-------------------------------

Checkout owner is determined at PDP / cart, not only at the checkout page — so price, shipping, duty, and tax presentation are correct before the customer commits.

* **SFCC owns:** AU domestic (including Oceania — Avalara for NZ + New Caledonia), UK, US (when shipping to US), EU domestic.
* **Global-e owns:** HK, ME, EU international, the US site when shipping outside the US, and any domestic storefront when the selected shipping destination is outside that storefront's market.
* **Pricing for Global-e markets (REG-041):** SFCC holds all pricebooks (including Global-e ones), derived nightly from AP21 base prices and Global-e FX/coefficients. SFCC sends the complete cart in target currency at handoff; Global-e owns shipping, duties, and tax from that point. Full mechanism specified under PRC-34..43.
* **Global-e shipping country lock (REG-028):** locked at the country selector pre-checkout; cannot change once inside Global-e.

7. Integration Map
------------------

### 7.1 Classification model

Every integration is placed in one of five **boundary classes** based on where its network call originates. The split is determined by the vendor's documented auth model — a publishable key implies browser-direct is safe; a secret key forces a server-side hop.

* **Browser-direct** — call originates from the user's browser. Vendor publishes a publishable/public key designed to ship in the JS bundle (with referrer or origin restrictions where applicable). No secret material is ever exposed.
* **MRT-mediated** — call originates from the Node layer that hosts PWA Kit (the SSR pass, a server-only proxy endpoint in the SSR/Node layer, the `/mobify/proxy/` forwarding layer, or a webhook receiver). Used whenever the vendor requires a secret token, whenever an API key must be kept off the browser bundle entirely, or whenever `httpOnly` cookies must be set or read. Credentials are held as MRT environment variables. This includes calls the PWA makes directly to MuleSoft via MRT proxy (rather than routing through SFCC).
* **SFCC-cartridge** — call originates from inside Salesforce Commerce Cloud (a Demandware cartridge). The PWA never makes the call; credentials live in SFCC Business Manager.
* **via MuleSoft** — SFCC-side, server-to-server through the MuleSoft middleware. The PWA never sees the downstream system.
* **Out-of-band** — runs outside the storefront runtime entirely (scheduled feed, build-time pipeline, or system-to-system integration that bypasses the PWA and often SFCC too).

A single integration can span multiple classes — e.g. Adyen is `SFCC-cartridge` for `/payments` calls and `Browser-direct` for the Drop-In SDK; Global-e is `Browser-direct` (checkout handoff — iframe embed) and `SFCC-cartridge` (pricing feed); GiveX is `via MuleSoft` / server-side NewStore-adapter for issue/validate/redeem/refund and `MRT-mediated` for balance checks. Compound rows list every class that applies.

> Reading the table: **Call origin** = where the network request is issued from. **Hosting layer** = which boundary class above. **Security** = how credentials are exposed.

8. SSR, SEO, and GEO Foundation
-------------------------------

### 8.1 SSR (DMU-030)

All product, category, and content pages will use SSR for full crawlability by search engines and AI bots without dependence on client-side JS. The PWA Kit SSR pipeline is preserved end-to-end. Componentry that cannot SSR is rendered through a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server. Global state stores are initialised per request to prevent state leaking across SSR responses.

#### 8.1.1 SSR vs CSR by page type

PWA Kit always runs the SSR pipeline — every page is server-rendered to some degree. The practical distinction is what content is rendered on the server vs fetched after hydration on the client.

| Page type | Pattern | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PDP, PLP, content pages, homepages, boutique pages | **Full SSR** — markup and data rendered on the server | Indexable, SEO- and LCP-critical |
| Cart, checkout, My Account, order history, wishlist, address book | **SSR shell + CSR data** — server renders the layout, header, footer, and skeleton; `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` hydrates personalised data (basket lines, customer profile, orders) client-side after hydration | Personalised, per-session, behind authentication. No SEO value (blocked in `robots.txt` — §8.3). Server-rendering personalised data would defeat edge caching and risk state leaking across requests |
| Search results, filtered PLP states | **SSR shell + CSR data** | Blocked in `robots.txt`; filter / sort state is client-driven |

The "SSR shell + CSR data" pattern still gives the user instant first paint of the page chrome — only the personalised payload waits on hydration. No page is purely client-rendered.

### 8.2 Canonicals & hreflang

Canonical tags on every indexable page; filtered PLPs canonicalise to the unfiltered base PLP. hreflang on canonical PDPs only, delivered via XML sitemap, consolidated to ~12 regional/language-level tags. Detailed canonical/hreflang rules are specified in the functional requirements.

### 8.3 Sitemaps & robots

Per-storefront / per-locale XML sitemaps refreshed daily, excluding disabled and deleted pages (DMU-026). `robots.txt` permits indexable pages (including the bag page) and blocks checkout, account, search results, and filtered URL parameters. URLs blocked in `robots.txt` never appear in a sitemap.

### 8.4 Structured data

Custom JSON-LD per the Sparro templates, rendered server-side so crawlers see it on the first response:

* **PDP:** Product + Merchant Listing Schema (`ProductGroup` + variant `Product`s), with real-time inventory driving availability.
* **PLP:** CollectionPage + BreadcrumbList + ItemList Schema (ItemList reflects the initial SSR'd product batch).
* **Boutique pages:** LocalBusiness / ClothingStore Schema per location.
* **Homepages:** Organisation + WebSite Schema per regional storefront, with per-prefix `WebSite` nodes (including the Global-e international paths `/en-ca/` and `/en-ch/`).

### 8.5 URL strategy

* Product URL: `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` — the `.html` suffix is preserved to maintain existing indexed URLs.
* Category URL: `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no suffix), with 301 redirects from legacy paths.
* 301 redirects for every URL that changes as a result of migration (products, categories, content). Implemented at the CDN/edge layer to keep application-layer impact minimal.

### 8.6 GEO (DMU-042)

No GEO-specific features in launch scope. The technical foundations enabling post-launch GEO — SSR, structured data, canonicals, XML sitemaps — are in place at go-live so no architecture decision blocks future activation.

9. Performance Strategy
-----------------------

LCP at p75 mobile is the binding constraint and the de-facto cap on third-party script weight.

| Metric | Target |
| --- | --- |
| LCP (mobile p75) | ≤ 2 s |
| Lighthouse Performance | ≥ 0.80 |
| Lighthouse Accessibility | ≥ 0.90 |
| Lighthouse Best Practices | ≥ 0.90 |

### 9.1 Third-party defer rule

Anything loaded via Didomi callback (GTM — which loads Meta, GA4, and other GTM-housed tags via Tell No Lies; Narvar EDD widget; Inside Chat) is deferred, async-loaded, or injected post-hydration so it does not block LCP. **Measmerize** (Find My Size / size guide — PDP only) likewise defers behind LCP — the script injects after the product hero image has loaded. **reCAPTCHA** likewise loads only on register/login form interaction, so it never sits on the critical path of any other page (consent treatment per §11.1). **Exception (AAB-004):** Optimizely Web is a PWA-direct head tag (not a GTM tag) and deliberately loads in the page head **before render** to prevent A/B flicker, scoped to the US storefront where Optimizely runs. **Crazy Egg (AAB-005)** loads async and post-Didomi-consent. Both load strictly post-Didomi-consent; keep both snippets minimal.

### 9.2 Other levers

* **Images:** all storefront imagery — product and editorial — is stored in and served from **Contentful** (`images.ctfassets.net`) via the Contentful Images API; SFCC holds no image assets (DMU-010 migration de-scoped; product images CRM-075; all media via the CMS library HPC-003). The PWA generates `srcset` / `sizes` and sets size, quality, and format per breakpoint on the asset URL — **AVIF primary with WebP / JPEG fallbacks**. Lazy-load all non-LCP images; priority-load the primary hero image (PRD-064). Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
* **Video:** sourced by platform, not self-hosted, so codec / adaptive-streaming selection belongs to the upstream player rather than to this layer:

  + **Product videos → Vimeo**, referenced by embed URL stored in product data or the CMS (PRD-067). Load behind a lightweight facade (poster image + click/scroll-to-load) so the Vimeo player JS never lands on the LCP critical path.
  + **Content-managed page videos → Contentful** by default, served from the Contentful asset CDN and referenced within the CMS content entry alongside the page content. Editorial pages may also embed a Vimeo video by URL where preferred (HPC-004) — the product/editorial split above is the expected pattern, not a hard restriction.
  + Across both: `preload="metadata"` by default; autoplay reserved for muted, short-loop hero clips only.
* Dynamic imports for heavy non-initial components.
* Parallel data fetches; no client-side waterfalls. Fetch only required fields.

### 9.3 Where performance is measured

The CI Lighthouse gate (§14.3) catches regressions but runs against the Dev-tier MRT deployment — slower than production hardware, further from the edge, and not representative of the LCP a real shopper experiences. The signed-off LCP and Lighthouse targets in this section are therefore validated against **Stage**, which mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle size class, same CDN/edge configuration, same SFCC realm tier). Treat CI numbers as regression indicators; treat Stage numbers as the contractual ones.

> **SSR connection pool tuning:** the initial per-pool connection caps defined in §12.1 are derived from expected concurrency, not observed traffic. The first Stage performance run should include per-pool queue-depth and connection-wait metrics (undici emits these as diagnostic channel events). Use those numbers to validate or revise the caps.

### 11.1 Didomi gating (REG-048–056)

In **all other regions** it loads on form interaction regardless of consent state.

| Omneo (writes) / Emarsys | Queue and retry silently; never block the user flow |
| Omneo (reads) | **Load-bearing for My Account profile pages** — per DMU-004 only email + Omneo ID are migrated; all other customer profile data is sourced live from Omneo at login. Surface an explicit retry/error UI on profile pages if the round-trip fails; do not render stale or partial profile data. |
| Google Maps | Degrade to manual address entry; never hard-block checkout |
| AP21 (Retail Rewards) | On AP21 unavailability at the point of Rewards application, inform the customer and allow an alternative payment method |
| Narvar (EDD) | Suppress widget; do not show an error or block checkout |

### 12.1 Blast-Radius Containment

The failure modes above describe what the PWA does when a single integration is unavailable. This section covers how to limit the *spread* of an attack or outage — ensuring a degraded integration cannot consume shared resources and take down unrelated features.

#### Edge (outside the PWA — Infrastructure / SI Partner)

* **Web Application Firewalls + rate limiting** is the primary lever for volumetric attacks and credential-stuffing.
* **SFCC Business Manager** provides API-level rate limiting for SFCC endpoints, independent of the storefront edge.

#### SSR layer (inside the PWA)

`overrides/app/ssr.js` makes server-side `fetch` calls directly (token exchange, JWKS, SF Payments metadata). Node's native `fetch` is backed by `undici` internally. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).

> **Implementation note:** the per-call `dispatcher` option is safer than the `setGlobalDispatcher` in a managed environment (MRT) since it does not touch the global dispatcher that Salesforce internal libraries may rely on. The `commerce-sdk-react` hooks manage their own HTTP client server-side (Commerce SDK) and are not affected in either approach.

The connection pool split is an engineering decision — the right pool boundaries and sizes depend on observed traffic patterns and the integration map in §7. Planned pools (connection caps should be validated later — see §9.3):

| Pool | Origin | Calls | Cap | `connectTimeout` | `bodyTimeout` | Reasoning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sfcc-scapi` | `<https://{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`> | SLAS JWKS (token validation for passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 8 s | `jose` caches the JWK set for its rotation period; actual network calls are rare. Isolated so a JWKS fetch is never starved by higher-volume pools. |
| `sfcc-payments` | `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` host (a `*.demandware.net` or SCAPI hostname — waiting confirmation from Mani) | Payment method metadata on every checkout page SSR | 10 | 5 s | 8 s | Called on every checkout page load; moderate frequency. Separate from `sfcc-scapi` because a checkout traffic spike must not consume SLAS connections. |
| `mulesoft` | `MULESOFT_BASE_URL` | Order history, order details, boutique / BOPIS stock check, GiveX balance check | 20 | 5 s | 10 s | Highest user-facing concurrency (My Account + PDP). GiveX balance calls carry payment credentials in the POST body — a slow MuleSoft response must not hold connections open and starve other pools. Highest cap reflects the broadest call surface. |
| `marketing-cloud-auth` | `<https://{subdomain}.auth.marketingcloudapis.com`> | Marketing Cloud client-credentials token exchange | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | User-triggered, infrequent; token cached at module scope for 15 min. Isolated so an MC outage cannot consume SFCC or MuleSoft connections. |
| `marketing-cloud-rest` | `<https://{subdomain}.rest.marketingcloudapis.com`> | Magic-link email send (passwordless login, reset password) | 5 | 5 s | 15 s | Same trigger as above; higher body timeout because email delivery APIs can respond slowly under load. |
| `google-places` | `<https://places.googleapis.com`> (Places API — New) | Address autocomplete at checkout (CFD-023, CFD-030, CFD-059) | 5 | 3 s | 5 s | Non-critical-path; graceful fallback to manual entry. Short timeouts ensure a Places API slowdown releases connections quickly. |
| `booxi` | Booxi base URL (TBD) | Boutique appointment read in My Account (CRM-165–167) | 5 | 3 s | 5 s | My Account only; non-critical-path within that page. |

**Contentful:** The Contentful SDK (`contentful` v11) does not expose a `dispatcher` hook on its internal fetch calls, so connection isolation for Contentful is not achievable through this pattern. Primary mitigation is the graceful degradation rule in §12 (Render page without editorial content).

---

13. Testing Strategy
--------------------

Three layers, no duplicated coverage — the cheapest layer that proves a behaviour wins.

| Layer | Tool | Covers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, isolated hooks |
| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | Single-component user interactions |
| E2E | Playwright | Full journeys, multi-region, integration boundaries |

### 13.1 What is tested

Failure paths that would be non-obvious or costly to debug: Contentful → component data mapping, locale / currency transforms, Global-e pricing / tax branching, checkout ownership, consent gating, cart mutations, optimistic-update rollback. Framework behaviour and pure visual rendering are not tested at this layer.

### 13.2 E2E gherkin-first workflow

Every Playwright spec starts as a Gherkin `.feature` file that Lead QA validates in plain English before any code is written. This prevents technically correct tests of the wrong behaviour.

### 13.3 Multi-region fixtures

E2E specs are parameterised by `SITE_ID` from day one — every journey runs across all 8 storefronts and 11 active locales, with site-specific `baseUrl`, currency, checkout owner, tax model, and consent default supplied by a fixture rather than hardcoded. (Because a test hardcoded to one region cannot be cheaply expanded later)

### 13.4 Selector priority

Tests select elements the way users and assistive tech perceive them: accessible selectors (role + name, label, visible text) first, semantic HTML attributes second (`alt`, `title`), `data-testid` only when nothing semantic applies. Tag/class/DOM-position selectors are not used. This doubles as a continuous accessibility check.

---

14. CI/CD & Environments
------------------------

This section probably belong to a DevOps TSD, but will put here temporarily until we have one.

### 14.1 Topology

A six-tier environment topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → Stage → UAT → Prod**. Each tier (other than Local) has its own SFCC realm, Contentful environment, and MuleSoft connections. Ownership splits across three zones — Digital, IT/NewStore, and Shared (Digital + Business).

| # | Tier | Owner | Purpose | Third-party availability | Deploy trigger |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Local** | Digital | Feature build on developer machines | All services mocked (MSW stubs) | `npm start` |
| 2 | **Dev** | Digital | Integrated digital testing across all 6 storefronts, independent of NewStore | MuleSoft STG · NewStore Dev · Omneo STG · Narvar stub · Adyen sandbox | Merge to `develop` |
| 3 | **SIT** | IT / NewStore | NewStore SIT and regression on its own cadence | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Narvar STG · AP21 test | NewStore release cadence (parallel lane, non-blocking for Digital releases) |
| 4 | **Stage** (E2E) | Shared | End-to-end testing with all third parties live; time-boxed booked windows | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Omneo STG · Narvar STG · Adyen sandbox | Booked 2-week window |
| 5 | **UAT** | Shared | Business acceptance across all 6 regions | NewStore STG · Narvar STG · Omneo STG · Adyen sandbox | Business approval gate |
| 6 | **Prod** | Live | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate |

Stage is the **contractual performance-test environment** referenced in §9.3 — it mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle class, CDN/edge configuration, SFCC realm tier).

### 14.2 Branch model

GitFlow with explicit back-merges to keep `develop` aligned with production.

| Branch | Branched from | Merges to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `feature/*` | `develop` | `develop` |
| `fix/*` | `develop` | `develop` |
| `release/*` | `develop` | `main` **and** `develop` |
| `fix/release-{version}-*` | the `release/*` branch | the `release/*` branch (forward-merged to `develop` via the release back-merge) |
| `hotfix/*` | `main` | `main` **and** `develop` |
| `develop`, `main` | — | protected; PR-only |

Release branches are supervised — code logic fixes go on a `fix/release-{version}-*` sub-branch rather than directly on the release branch. Releases and hotfixes always back-merge to `develop` so production fixes flow forward automatically.

### 14.3 CI workflows

**QA workflow (**`qa.yml`) — runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`. Code-correctness checks with no environment dependency:

* Unit tests (Vitest)
* Storybook interaction tests (`play` functions) and component-level accessibility checks via `@storybook/addon-a11y` (`storybook test --ci`)

**SIT gate (**`digital-sit.yml`) — runs on push/PR to `release/**`; on merge to `develop` it also deploys to the **Dev** environment (tier 2 in §14.1). Environment-dependent checks:

* Playwright `p0` priority specs
* Bundle-size check against the ceilings in §9
* Contract tests against the MuleSoft OpenAPI specification
* Lighthouse CI thresholds (Performance ≥ 0.80, Accessibility ≥ 0.90, Best Practices ≥ 0.90)
* Trend gate against the LHCI history server

### 14.4 Deployment

Deployment is via Salesforce Managed Runtime. Each tier maps to its own MRT target:

* **Dev** — deployed on merge to `develop`, gated on a clean SIT gate (§14.3)
* **SIT** — deployed on the NewStore release cadence, isolated from the Digital release path (failures do not block `release/**`)
* **Stage** — deployed on a booked 2-week window for full end-to-end testing with live third parties
* **UAT** — deployed for business acceptance; promotion requires Business sign-off
* **Prod** — release-manager-gated; AU canary first, then flag-flip to remaining regions

Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through Stage and UAT.

MRT deployment targets map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | stage | uat | production`.",

      "value": "1-overview1. Overview
---------------------

Product data in the Zimmermann SFCC platform is managed through a **master catalogue** (`zimmermann-catalog`) with per-site **storefront catalogues** for navigation and category assignment. Product content (rich text, editorial imagery) is managed in **Contentful CMS**.

AP21 is the system of record for all product data. Product data flows from AP21 into SFCC via **MuleSoft** — there is no direct AP21 → SFCC integration. MuleSoft acts as the integration layer, transforming and routing product data into SFCC catalogue XML imports.

---

2-product-data-architecture2. Product Data Architecture
-------------------------------------------------------

DefaultnoneAP21 (ERP — system of record for products)
│
└──► MuleSoft (integration layer — transform + route)
│
└──► zimmermann-catalog (SFCC master catalogue)
│ products + variants + attributes
│
├──► zimmermann-au-storefront-catalog (AU nav categories)
├──► zimmermann-uk-storefront-catalog (UK nav categories)
├──► zimmermann-us-storefront-catalog (US domestic nav categories)
├──► zimmermann-us-intl-storefront-catalog (US International / Global-e nav categories)
├──► zimmermann-eu-storefront-catalog (EU nav categories)
├──► zimmermann-eu-intl-storefront-catalog (EU International / Global-e nav categories)
├──► zimmermann-hk-storefront-catalog (HK nav categories)
└──► zimmermann-me-storefront-catalog (ME nav categories)
Contentful CMS
│
└──► PWA Kit (editorial content: banners, editorial copy, lookbook)
via Contentful Delivery API

9-key-design-decisions9. Key Design Decisions
---------------------------------------------

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Product source of truth | AP21 | AP21 is the ERP and master for all product data |
| Product integration layer | MuleSoft | Consistent with Zimmermann integration platform; MuleSoft handles AP21 event consumption, transformation, and SFCC delivery |
| Product imagery | Loaded directly into SFCC | No external DAM or Cloudinary in the pipeline; images stored in SFCC static content library |
| Catalogue structure | One master + eight storefront catalogues | SFCC best practice for multi-site |
| Editorial content | Contentful | Decouples editorial from product data; supports headless PWA pattern |
| Category positions | Explicit `<position>` elements per category | Ensures nav order matches Figma design across all sites |
| USIntl separate storefront catalogue | `zimmermann-us-intl-storefront-catalog` | Allows independent category assignment for Global-e international customers |

**Objective:** Document the MRT (Managed Runtime) APIs available for product, category, and pricing data so the squad knows what can be built and tested in **lower environments** while MuleSoft isn't ready.

**Background (verbatim intent):** Mani has the base BM config in place, but product/price data is missing because MuleSoft isn't ready. *"Angelo to set up session with Mani."* → **Angelo = you; Mani = Manikandan Ramachandran**, who owns the SFCC-1 "Platform Setup & Environments" epic.

**DoD:** A documented inventory of relevant MRT APIs, shared with the squad, sufficient to **unblock BM configuration and front-end dev in lower environments**.

---

## The crux (this reframes the whole spike)

**"MRT" is the PWA Kit hosting/proxy layer, not an API.** The data the spike cares about reaches the PWA through **SCAPI (Shopper APIs)** proxied *via* MRT — not through MuleSoft. Confirmed against the live codebase:

- `zimmermann-pwa` is PWA Kit **3.18.0** on template extensibility over `@salesforce/retail-react-app` 10.0.0, consuming SFCC exclusively through **`@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` 5.2.0** hooks (`useProduct`, `useProductSearch`, …).
- MRT proxies two backends (`config/default.js:206-218`): **`api` → SCAPI** (shortCode `qmyt7hks`) and **`ocapi` → dev sandbox** (`bkzk-002`). Auth is **SLAS private-client**, secret held server-side.
- **MuleSoft does *not* serve product/category/pricing to the PWA.** Per `.docs/integration/03-mulesoft.md`, the PWA→MRT→MuleSoft path is only orders, returns, and real-time boutique stock. Product/price master data is an explicitly **server-to-server** AP21 → MuleSoft → SFCC catalogue/pricebook feed (`03-mulesoft.md:24-25`).

**So SCAPI is fully capable of serving product/category/pricing right now.** The blocker isn't API capability — it's that **SFCC has no catalog/price data yet**, because the MuleSoft feed that populates it hasn't been built (SFCC-121, Victor, "Ready for Development"). That's the real message the spike needs to land with the squad.

---

## MRT API inventory (the deliverable content, already 80% in-repo)

**A. Consumption path — SCAPI Shopper APIs via MRT** (from `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md §4`):

| Resource | Serves | Verbs |
|---|---|---|
| `/product/shopper-products/v1/*` | Product detail, master/variant resolution | GET |
| `/search/shopper-search/v1/*` | Category listing, search, faceting, sort, suggestions | GET |
| `/pricing/shopper-promotions/v1/*` | Active promotions, coupon validation | GET |
| `/checkout/shopper-login/oauth2/*` | SLAS auth / token lifecycle | GET, POST |
| (+ baskets v2, orders v1, customers v1) | Cart, checkout, account | — |

Pricing specifics are proven in code — `home/index.tsx:52-60` runs `useProductSearch` with `expand: ['promotions','variations','prices',…]`, `perPricebook: true`, category refinement via `cgid`. So price-book-aware pricing + category browse work as soon as data exists.

**B. Fallback path — OCAPI via MRT:** anything SCAPI doesn't cover is proxied server-side with OCAPI credentials (`01-sfcc.md:52`).

**C. Population path (the missing piece) — server-to-server, not PWA:** AP21 → MuleSoft → SFCC via **OCAPI Data API** (`/s/-/dw/data/v*/catalogs`) or SFTP import job (Confluence TSD Product 292061208 §4.2). Master `zimmermann-catalog` + 8 storefront catalogs; IDs are `stylecode` (master) / `stylecode+colourcode+sizecode` (variant).

---

## What unblocks lower environments

Since SCAPI works but SFCC is empty, the unblock is to **load catalog + pricebook data into the sandbox** (via BM or OCAPI Data API) so the PWA can read it through SCAPI without waiting for MuleSoft.

⚠️ **Accuracy flag:** the sample-catalog tooling (`data/sample/catalogs`, `data:import:sample`) referenced in the Confluence TSD is **not in `zimmermann-pwa`** — I checked; there's no `data/` dir, no `dw.json`, and only `syncRegionalConfig.mjs` under `scripts/sfcc`. That tooling lives in the separate **`zimmermann-sfccworkplace`** cartridge repo (per TSD 292061208 §11). The PWA repo only *consumes*. This is exactly what the **session with Mani** needs to resolve: who loads sample/real data into the `bkzk-002` sandbox, and how.

---

## Permanent vs workaround (Task 4)

- **Permanent:** SCAPI-via-MRT for all product/category/pricing consumption; MuleSoft catalogue/pricebook feed for population; OCAPI-via-MRT as the fallback for gaps.
- **Workaround (current state only):** manual / sample catalog + pricebook load into the sandbox to unblock dev before the AP21→MuleSoft feed exists.

---

## Gaps & dependencies to name in the doc

- **No catalog/price data in the sandbox** until either sample data is loaded or MuleSoft delivers (SFCC-121 dependency).
- MuleSoft **rate limits** for real-time calls still unconfirmed (Confluence 320602113, G3).
- Per-environment SLAS client ID / short code partly outstanding (`01-sfcc.md §7`).
- Delivery mechanism (OCAPI Data API vs SFTP) and feed trigger still open (TSD 292061208, open item #1).

**Sources:** codebase `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` & `03-mulesoft.md`; Confluence SFCC space pages 292061208 (Product), 292388871 (Price), 320602113 (MuleSoft Open Questions), 256835585 (TSD PWA), 264896514 (Headless build/deploy). Saved a memory of the key findings for future sessions.

---

2. **Prep the Mani session** — a tight agenda + question list (sandbox data loading, who owns `zimmermann-sfccworkplace`, delivery mechanism).
3. **Verify live** — the sandbox SCAPI is reachable at `qmyt7hks.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`; I could sketch a guest-token + shopper-search probe to confirm whether any catalog data exists yet in `bkzk-002`.

# SFCC-122 — SFCC MRT API Capabilities

**Spike deliverable · Squad-A**

| | |
|---|---|
| Jira | SFCC-122 (Spike, High, In Progress) |
| Assignee | Marcel Angelo Navarro |
| Reporter | Jasmijn Tsang |
| Related | SFCC-121 (Validate MuleSoft Sync), SFCC-123 (Contentful design), SFCC-1 (Platform Setup & Environments, owner: M. Ramachandran) |
| Status of this doc | Draft for squad review |
| Last updated | 2026-07-22 |

---

## TL;DR

1. **"MRT" is the hosting and proxy layer, not an API.** Managed Runtime is the PWA Kit Node server. The APIs the storefront actually consumes for product, category, and pricing data are **SCAPI (Salesforce Commerce API, the Shopper APIs)**, reached *through* the MRT proxy.
2. **SCAPI can already serve product, category, and pricing today.** The capability exists now: `shopper-products`, `shopper-search`, and `shopper-promotions` are wired and proven in the codebase.
3. **The blocker is empty data, not a missing API.** Product and price data are absent from the lower environments because the AP21 -> MuleSoft -> SFCC catalogue and pricebook feed has not been built yet. That is a data-population problem, owned server-side, not an MRT/SCAPI capability gap.
4. **MuleSoft does not serve product or pricing to the PWA.** The direct PWA -> MRT -> MuleSoft path is only for orders, returns, and real-time boutique stock. Product and price master data is a separate server-to-server import into SFCC.
5. **To unblock lower-environment build and test now:** load catalog and pricebook data into the `bkzk-002` sandbox (Business Manager or the OCAPI Data API), confirm BM site/catalog/pricebook assignment, then the PWA consumes it via SCAPI with no code change.

---

## 1. Objective

Document the SFCC MRT (Managed Runtime) APIs relevant to the Zimmermann storefront build, so the squad has a clear picture of what is available for product, pricing, and category data consumption before MuleSoft is ready. This lets the squad determine what can be built and tested in lower environments in the meantime.

## 2. Background

- Base Business Manager configuration is in place on the SFCC sandbox, but product and price data are currently missing because MuleSoft is not yet ready.
- Understanding the MRT API capabilities tells the squad what can be built and tested in lower environments while that feed is being built.
- Session to be set up with M. Ramachandran (owner of SFCC-1, Platform Setup & Environments) to confirm the sandbox data-loading approach.
- The storefront is a PWA Kit application (`zimmermann-pwa`) hosted on Managed Runtime, template-extending `@salesforce/retail-react-app`, consuming commerce data from SFCC and editorial content from Contentful.

## 3. Tasks and findings

### 3.1 Task 1 — Review and document the available MRT APIs

**How commerce data reaches the storefront.** The browser talks to SFCC through a proxy hosted by Managed Runtime. Nothing calls SFCC directly from a hard-coded backend host; every call goes through an MRT proxy path, which lets MRT attach server-only credentials and keeps secrets out of the browser bundle.

```
Browser (React, SSR + CSR)
   │  @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react (TanStack Query under the hood)
   ▼
MRT proxy  /mobify/proxy/api    ──►  SCAPI  (Shopper APIs)      ← product, category, price, search, promotions, basket, orders, customers
           /mobify/proxy/ocapi  ──►  OCAPI  (fallback + Data API)
           /mobify/proxy/mulesoft ─► MuleSoft (orders, returns, boutique stock ONLY — designed, not yet wired)
   ▼
SFCC realm (sandbox bkzk-002 in Dev)
```

The single SDK `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (v5.2.0) handles every SFCC call: SLAS token lifecycle, retry, and TanStack Query caching. Verified in `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx` (CommerceApiProvider wiring) and consumed via hooks such as `useProduct` and `useProductSearch`.

#### 3.1.1 SCAPI Shopper APIs (primary path for product, category, pricing)

Reached at MRT proxy path `/mobify/proxy/api` (`config/default.js:131`). These are the APIs that serve the data this spike is about.

| API family | Path root | Serves | Verbs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shopper Products | `/product/shopper-products/v1/*` | Product detail, master/variant resolution, images, prices on the product | GET |
| Shopper Search | `/search/shopper-search/v1/*` | Category product listing (`cgid` refinement), keyword search, faceting, sort, suggestions | GET |
| Shopper Promotions | `/pricing/shopper-promotions/v1/*` | Active promotions, coupon validation | GET |
| Shopper Login (SLAS) | `/checkout/shopper-login/oauth2/*` | Guest and registered auth, token lifecycle | GET, POST |
| Shopper Baskets | `/checkout/shopper-baskets/v2/*` | Basket / cart lifecycle, line items | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE |
| Shopper Orders | `/checkout/shopper-orders/v1/*` | Order placement and lookup (SFCC-owned checkouts) | POST, GET |
| Shopper Customers | `/customer/shopper-customers/v1/*` | Profile, addresses, saved-payment references | GET, POST, PATCH |

Source: `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` section 4.

**Pricing is fully supported through SCAPI.** The canonical query in the codebase (`overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx`) uses `useProductSearch` with `refine: ['cgid=<categoryId>', 'htype=master']` and `expand: ['promotions','variations','prices','images','custom_properties']`, `perPricebook: true`, `allVariationProperties: true`. This demonstrates category refinement plus pricebook-aware pricing and promotion expansion working end to end, given data exists.

#### 3.1.2 Endpoint structure, base URL, and environments

- **SCAPI base host:** `{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`, proxied via `/mobify/proxy/api`. Verified: `config/default.js:210` host `qmyt7hks.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`.
- **Instance identifiers** (non-secret; injected from env into the SDK provider at `config/default.js:132-137`):
  - `shortCode`: `qmyt7hks`
  - `organizationId`: `f_ecom_bkzk_002` (realm/instance `bkzk_002`)
  - `siteId`: `ZimmermannAU` (default; nine sites total, see `config/sites.js`)
  - `clientId`: SLAS client ID (public identifier, held in `COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID`)
- **Per-environment config:** `config/dev.js`, `test.js`, `sit.js`, `staging.js`, `uat.js`, `production.js` each override `proxyConfigs`. The SCAPI host stays constant (`qmyt7hks...`); the OCAPI host changes per tier (Dev -> `bkzk-002.dx...`, Prod -> `production-ap01-zimmermann.demandware.net`).
- **Env switching:** `npm run env -- <tier>` (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`); deploy per tier via `npm run push:<tier>` -> `pwa-kit-dev push -t <target>`.
- MRT environment variables are managed per environment in the Managed Runtime console and rotated independently of the codebase (Confluence: Technical Solution Design - PWA).

#### 3.1.3 Authentication

- **SLAS private-client flow** issues a guest access token (anonymous shopper, refreshed silently) and a registered shopper token (after email/password login). Tokens are JWTs carrying customer ID, unique shopper ID (USID), and a refresh token.
- **Secrets stay server-side.** The SLAS client secret is an MRT environment variable and never reaches the browser; the authorisation-code exchange is proxied through the MRT private-client endpoint. The SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code remain in the bundle as public identifiers. Confirmed in `overrides/app/ssr.js` (`useSLASPrivateClient: true`).
- **Refresh tokens** live in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies set by the SSR layer; browser JavaScript never sees the raw refresh token.
- **Multi-site tokens are channel-scoped.** A token for one site is not valid for another; a storefront switch triggers a fresh server-side authorisation (SLAS Trusted System on Behalf).

Source: `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` section 3.

#### 3.1.4 Payload format and query conventions

- **Format:** JSON over HTTPS (TLS 1.2+), standard SCAPI response envelopes.
- **Every request carries** site ID, organisation ID, locale, currency, and the SLAS bearer token.
- **Efficiency levers used:** `expand=` to pull promotions/variations/prices/images in one call; `fields=` projection to trim payloads; `perPricebook: true` for pricebook-aware pricing; TanStack Query dedup and caching (catalogue stale time ~60s, promotions ~30s, basket 0s).

#### 3.1.5 OCAPI (fallback and Data API)

- Reached at MRT proxy path `/mobify/proxy/ocapi` (`config/default.js:213-216`, Dev host `bkzk-002.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com`).
- Purpose: anything not yet covered by SCAPI is proxied through MRT with OCAPI credentials held server-side. No OCAPI credentials ever reach the browser.
- The **OCAPI Data API** (`/s/-/dw/data/v*/catalogs`) is also the server-side channel used to import catalogue data into SFCC (see 3.1.8).

#### 3.1.6 MuleSoft-direct reads via MRT (not product, category, or pricing)

There is a designed direct path `PWA -> MRT -> MuleSoft` at `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...` for a small set of reads where SFCC adds nothing to the round-trip. It is **scaffolded but not yet wired into `proxyConfigs`** (no `mulesoft` entry in any `config/*.js`; an undici connection pool exists at `overrides/app/ssr/connectionPools.ts`).

In scope for this path: order history list, order detail, returns, real-time boutique stock (Find in Boutique / BOPIS), GiveX balance check. **Product, category, and pricing are explicitly out of scope for this path.** Source: `.docs/integration/03-mulesoft.md`.

#### 3.1.7 Einstein recommendations (adjacent capability)

Personalised recommendations use the Einstein API (`config/default.js:140-148`, host `api.cquotient.com`), consent-gated, with a static SFCC merchandising-group fallback. Not part of the core product/category/pricing consumption but available through the same app.

#### 3.1.8 Catalogue and pricebook population path (server-to-server, the missing piece)

This is what "MuleSoft is not yet ready" refers to, and it is not an MRT capability at all:

- **Product:** AP21 (ERP, system of record) -> MuleSoft (transform to SFCC Catalog XML) -> SFCC, delivered via the **OCAPI Data API** (`/s/-/dw/data/v*/catalogs`) or SFTP + import job. Master catalogue `zimmermann-catalog` plus per-site storefront catalogues.
- **Price:** AP21 -> SFCC pricebooks (per-site, per-currency), delivery mechanism to be confirmed (see open items).
- Product IDs: master = `stylecode` (e.g. `4673TS251`); variant = `stylecode + colourcode + sizecode`.
- The master-catalogue-to-storefront-category assignment is set in Business Manager and cannot be set via XML import.

Source: Confluence "TSD: Product — SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration" and "TSD: Price — SFCC Pricebooks & Global-e".

### 3.2 Task 2 — Which MRT APIs can serve product, category, and pricing in lower environments now

**Answer: SCAPI can, as soon as data exists in the sandbox.** The API capability is not the constraint. `shopper-products`, `shopper-search` (with `cgid` category refinement), and pricebook-aware pricing via `expand=prices&perPricebook=true` all work against any populated SFCC instance.

The only thing missing in the lower environments is **data in the SFCC catalogue and pricebooks**. Once data is loaded (see section 4), front-end development and testing can proceed against SCAPI with no dependency on the MuleSoft feed being finished.

| Capability | Available in lower env now? | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| Product detail (`shopper-products`) | Yes, once catalogue data is loaded | Sandbox catalogue populated |
| Category listing / search (`shopper-search`, `cgid`) | Yes, once catalogue + storefront categories + search index exist | BM catalogue assignment + search index rebuild |
| Pricing (`prices`, `perPricebook`) | Yes, once pricebooks are loaded and assigned | Sandbox pricebooks populated + assigned to site |
| Promotions (`shopper-promotions`) | Yes, once promotions are configured in BM | BM promotion setup |
| Auth (SLAS) | Yes, working now | SLAS client already configured |

### 3.3 Task 3 — Limitations and gaps to be covered by MuleSoft (or elsewhere)

- **No catalogue or price data in the sandbox** until either sample/manual data is loaded or the AP21 -> MuleSoft -> SFCC feed is built (dependency: SFCC-121).
- **Catalogue/price freshness and delta handling** (event vs scheduled, sale-price removal signals) are MuleSoft-feed concerns, not SCAPI concerns.
- **MuleSoft real-time rate limits** for the direct-read path are unconfirmed (Confluence "MuleSoft Integration — Open Questions", item G3).
- **Delivery mechanism for catalogue import** (OCAPI Data API vs SFTP + import job) and the feed trigger are still open (Confluence TSD Product, open item 1).
- **Per-environment SLAS client ID / short code** for non-Dev tiers partly outstanding (`.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` section 7).
- The **MuleSoft direct-read proxy** (`/mobify/proxy/mulesoft`) is not yet wired, so order history, returns, and boutique stock are not consumable from the PWA until it is added and MuleSoft endpoints are provisioned per environment.

### 3.4 Task 4 — Permanent architecture vs current-state workaround

| Element | Classification | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| SCAPI via MRT proxy for product / category / pricing consumption | **Permanent** | The storefront's supported model for all shopper data |
| SLAS private-client auth via MRT | **Permanent** | Standard PWA Kit pattern |
| AP21 -> MuleSoft -> SFCC catalogue and pricebook feed (population) | **Permanent** | The intended data source; not yet built |
| OCAPI via MRT for operations SCAPI does not cover | **Permanent (semi)** | Fallback by design; shrinks as SCAPI coverage grows |
| PWA -> MRT -> MuleSoft direct reads (orders, returns, boutique stock) | **Permanent** | Designed, not yet wired |
| Manual / sample catalogue and pricebook load into the sandbox | **Workaround** | Current-state only, to unblock lower-env build and test before the MuleSoft feed exists |

## 4. Recommended actions to unblock lower environments

1. **Load catalogue and pricebook data into the `bkzk-002` sandbox.** Options, in order of preference for a quick unblock:
   - Import a sample/seed catalogue + pricebooks via the **OCAPI Data API** (`/s/-/dw/data/v*/catalogs`) or a site-archive import job in Business Manager.
   - Note: the catalogue/data tooling and sample data are **not in `zimmermann-pwa`** (the PWA repo only consumes). Per the TSD, the conversion/seed tooling lives in the separate `zimmermann-sfccworkplace` cartridge repo. Confirm ownership and access with M. Ramachandran.
2. **Confirm Business Manager configuration** on the sandbox: site catalogue assignment (`ZimmermannAU` -> `zimmermann-au-storefront-catalog`), storefront category tree, pricebook assignment per site/currency, and a search index rebuild so `shopper-search` returns results.
3. **Verify SCAPI reachability** from the sandbox with a SLAS guest token and a `shopper-search` smoke test, to confirm data is queryable before front-end work starts.
4. **Front-end proceeds via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`** hooks against the populated sandbox: no code change is needed once data exists.
5. **Track the permanent feed** (SFCC-121) separately; the workaround load is throwaway once the AP21 -> MuleSoft -> SFCC feed is delivering.

## 5. Definition of Done — status

> **DoD:** A documented inventory of relevant MRT APIs is produced and shared with the squad, sufficient to unblock BM configuration and front-end development in lower environments.

| DoD element | Status |
|---|---|
| Inventory of relevant MRT/SCAPI APIs (endpoints, structure, payload, auth, data) | Done — section 3.1 |
| Assessment of what can serve product/category/pricing in lower envs | Done — section 3.2 |
| Limitations and gaps for MuleSoft to cover | Done — section 3.3 |
| Permanent vs workaround classification | Done — section 3.4 |
| Actions sufficient to unblock BM config and front-end dev | Done — section 4 |
| Shared with the squad | Pending — this draft to be reviewed, then published to Confluence |

## 6. Open questions (for M. Ramachandran / integration team)

1. What product / category / price data (if any) is currently loaded in the `bkzk-002` sandbox, and how did it get there?
2. Who owns the `zimmermann-sfccworkplace` cartridge repo and the sample/seed catalogue data, and can we get access to run an import?
3. Preferred sandbox load mechanism for the interim: OCAPI Data API, BM site-archive import, or manual BM entry?
4. Is the base BM config (site catalogue assignment, pricebook assignment, search index) already complete on the sandbox, or is any of it outstanding?
5. Confirmed delivery mechanism and trigger for the permanent AP21 -> MuleSoft -> SFCC catalogue and price feed (ties to SFCC-121).

## Appendix A — Config reference (verified in code)

| Item | Value / location |
|---|---|
| PWA Kit runtime | `@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime` / `-react-sdk` 3.18.0 |
| Base template | `@salesforce/retail-react-app` 10.0.0 (template extensibility, `overrides/`) |
| Commerce SDK | `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` 5.2.0 |
| Commerce API params | `config/default.js:130-138` |
| Proxy configs | `config/default.js:206-218` (`api` -> SCAPI, `ocapi` -> sandbox) |
| SSR / SLAS private client | `overrides/app/ssr.js` |
| SCAPI host (Dev) | `qmyt7hks.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com` |
| OCAPI host (Dev) | `bkzk-002.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com` |
| Org / site (Dev) | `f_ecom_bkzk_002` / `ZimmermannAU` |
| Secrets | Held as MRT env vars / local `.env` (gitignored); never in the browser bundle |

## Appendix B — Sources

- Codebase (`zimmermann-pwa`): `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md`, `.docs/integration/03-mulesoft.md`, `config/default.js`, `config/*.js`, `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/ssr/connectionPools.ts`, `package.json`.

#### 3.1.4 Payload format and query conventions

- **Format:** JSON over HTTPS (TLS 1.2+), standard SCAPI response envelopes.
- **Every request carries** site ID, organisation ID, locale, currency, and the SLAS bearer token.
- **Efficiency levers used:** `expand=` to pull promotions/variations/prices/images in one call; `fields=` projection to trim payloads; `perPricebook: true` for pricebook-aware pricing; TanStack Query dedup and caching (catalogue stale time ~60s, promotions ~30s, basket 0s).

#### 3.1.5 OCAPI (fallback and Data API)

- Reached at MRT proxy path `/mobify/proxy/ocapi` (`config/default.js:213-216`, Dev host `bkzk-002.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com`).
- Purpose: anything not yet covered by SCAPI is proxied through MRT with OCAPI credentials held server-side. No OCAPI credentials ever reach the browser.
- The **OCAPI Data API** (`/s/-/dw/data/v*/catalogs`) is also the server-side channel used to import catalogue data into SFCC (see 3.1.8).

#### 3.1.6 MuleSoft-direct reads via MRT (not product, category, or pricing)

There is a designed direct path `PWA -> MRT -> MuleSoft` at `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...` for a small set of reads where SFCC adds nothing to the round-trip. It is **scaffolded but not yet wired into `proxyConfigs`** (no `mulesoft` entry in any `config/*.js`; an undici connection pool exists at `overrides/app/ssr/connectionPools.ts`).

In scope for this path: order history list, order detail, returns, real-time boutique stock (Find in Boutique / BOPIS), GiveX balance check. **Product, category, and pricing are explicitly out of scope for this path.** Source: `.docs/integration/03-mulesoft.md`.

#### 3.1.7 Einstein recommendations (adjacent capability)

Personalised recommendations use the Einstein API (`config/default.js:140-148`, host `api.cquotient.com`), consent-gated, with a static SFCC merchandising-group fallback. Not part of the core product/category/pricing consumption but available through the same app.

#### 3.1.8 Catalogue and pricebook population path (server-to-server, the missing piece)

This is what "MuleSoft is not yet ready" refers to, and it is not an MRT capability at all:

- **Product:** AP21 (ERP, system of record) -> MuleSoft (transform to SFCC Catalog XML) -> SFCC, delivered via the **OCAPI Data API** (`/s/-/dw/data/v*/catalogs`) or SFTP + import job. Master catalogue `zimmermann-catalog` plus per-site storefront catalogues.
- **Price:** AP21 -> SFCC pricebooks (per-site, per-currency), delivery mechanism to be confirmed (see open items).
- Product IDs: master = `stylecode` (e.g. `4673TS251`); variant = `stylecode + colourcode + sizecode`.
- The master-catalogue-to-storefront-category assignment is set in Business Manager and cannot be set via XML import.

Source: Confluence "TSD: Product — SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration" and "TSD: Price — SFCC Pricebooks & Global-e".

### 3.2 Task 2 — Which MRT APIs can serve product, category, and pricing in lower environments now

**Answer: SCAPI can, as soon as data exists in the sandbox.** The API capability is not the constraint. `shopper-products`, `shopper-search` (with `cgid` category refinement), and pricebook-aware pricing via `expand=prices&perPricebook=true` all work against any populated SFCC instance.

The only thing missing in the lower environments is **data in the SFCC catalogue and pricebooks**. Once data is loaded (see section 4), front-end development and testing can proceed against SCAPI with no dependency on the MuleSoft feed being finished.

| Capability | Available in lower env now? | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| Product detail (`shopper-products`) | Yes, once catalogue data is loaded | Sandbox catalogue populated |
| Category listing / search (`shopper-search`, `cgid`) | Yes, once catalogue + storefront categories + search index exist | BM catalogue assignment + search index rebuild |
| Pricing (`prices`, `perPricebook`) | Yes, once pricebooks are loaded and assigned | Sandbox pricebooks populated + assigned to site |
| Promotions (`shopper-promotions`) | Yes, once promotions are configured in BM | BM promotion setup |
| Auth (SLAS) | Yes, working now | SLAS client already configured |

### 3.3 Task 3 — Limitations and gaps to be covered by MuleSoft (or elsewhere)

- **No catalogue or price data in the sandbox** until either sample/manual data is loaded or the AP21 -> MuleSoft -> SFCC feed is built (dependency: SFCC-121).
- **Catalogue/price freshness and delta handling** (event vs scheduled, sale-price removal signals) are MuleSoft-feed concerns, not SCAPI concerns.
- **MuleSoft real-time rate limits** for the direct-read path are unconfirmed (Confluence "MuleSoft Integration — Open Questions", item G3).
- **Delivery mechanism for catalogue import** (OCAPI Data API vs SFTP + import job) and the feed trigger are still open (Confluence TSD Product, open item 1).
- **Per-environment SLAS client ID / short code** for non-Dev tiers partly outstanding (`.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` section 7).
- The **MuleSoft direct-read proxy** (`/mobify/proxy/mulesoft`) is not yet wired, so order history, returns, and boutique stock are not consumable from the PWA until it is added and MuleSoft endpoints are provisioned per environment.

### 3.4 Task 4 — Permanent architecture vs current-state workaround

| Element | Classification | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| SCAPI via MRT proxy for product / category / pricing consumption | **Permanent** | The storefront's supported model for all shopper data |
| SLAS private-client auth via MRT | **Permanent** | Standard PWA Kit pattern |
| AP21 -> MuleSoft -> SFCC catalogue and pricebook feed (population) | **Permanent** | The intended data source; not yet built |
| OCAPI via MRT for operations SCAPI does not cover | **Permanent (semi)** | Fallback by design; shrinks as SCAPI coverage grows |
| PWA -> MRT -> MuleSoft direct reads (orders, returns, boutique stock) | **Permanent** | Designed, not yet wired |
| Manual / sample catalogue and pricebook load into the sandbox | **Workaround** | Current-state only, to unblock lower-env build and test before the MuleSoft feed exists |

## 4. Recommended actions to unblock lower environments

1. **Load catalogue and pricebook data into the `bkzk-002` sandbox.** Options, in order of preference for a quick unblock:
   - Import a sample/seed catalogue + pricebooks via the **OCAPI Data API** (`/s/-/dw/data/v*/catalogs`) or a site-archive import job in Business Manager.
   - Note: the catalogue/data tooling and sample data are **not in `zimmermann-pwa`** (the PWA repo only consumes). Per the TSD, the conversion/seed tooling lives in the separate `zimmermann-sfccworkplace` cartridge repo. Confirm ownership and access with M. Ramachandran.
2. **Confirm Business Manager configuration** on the sandbox: site catalogue assignment (`ZimmermannAU` -> `zimmermann-au-storefront-catalog`), storefront category tree, pricebook assignment per site/currency, and a search index rebuild so `shopper-search` returns results.
3. **Verify SCAPI reachability** from the sandbox with a SLAS guest token and a `shopper-search` smoke test, to confirm data is queryable before front-end work starts.
4. **Front-end proceeds via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`** hooks against the populated sandbox: no code change is needed once data exists.
5. **Track the permanent feed** (SFCC-121) separately; the workaround load is throwaway once the AP21 -> MuleSoft -> SFCC feed is delivering.

## 5. Definition of Done — status

> **DoD:** A documented inventory of relevant MRT APIs is produced and shared with the squad, sufficient to unblock BM configuration and front-end development in lower environments.

| DoD element | Status |
|---|---|
| Inventory of relevant MRT/SCAPI APIs (endpoints, structure, payload, auth, data) | Done — section 3.1 |
| Assessment of what can serve product/category/pricing in lower envs | Done — section 3.2 |
| Limitations and gaps for MuleSoft to cover | Done — section 3.3 |
| Permanent vs workaround classification | Done — section 3.4 |
| Actions sufficient to unblock BM config and front-end dev | Done — section 4 |
| Shared with the squad | Pending — this draft to be reviewed, then published to Confluence |

## 6. Open questions (for M. Ramachandran / integration team)

1. What product / category / price data (if any) is currently loaded in the `bkzk-002` sandbox, and how did it get there?
2. Who owns the `zimmermann-sfccworkplace` cartridge repo and the sample/seed catalogue data, and can we get access to run an import?
3. Preferred sandbox load mechanism for the interim: OCAPI Data API, BM site-archive import, or manual BM entry?
4. Is the base BM config (site catalogue assignment, pricebook assignment, search index) already complete on the sandbox, or is any of it outstanding?
5. Confirmed delivery mechanism and trigger for the permanent AP21 -> MuleSoft -> SFCC catalogue and price feed (ties to SFCC-121).

# Review: SFCC-122 — SFCC MRT API Capabilities

## Part A — Code-claim verification ledger

Every code-derived claim in the document was opened and checked against source. Summary:

**CONFIRMED (accurate against code):**

| Claim (doc location) | Verified against |
|---|---|
| `commerceAPI` params at `config/default.js:130-138`; `proxyPath: '/mobify/proxy/api'` at :131 | `config/default.js:130-138`, :131 exact match |
| params injected from env at `:132-137` (clientId, organizationId, shortCode, siteId) | `config/default.js:132-137` exact |
| `proxyConfigs` at `:206-218`, `api`→SCAPI, `ocapi`→sandbox | array is `:208-217` (range is slightly loose but correct) |
| SCAPI host `qmyt7hks.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com` at `:210` | exact |
| OCAPI Dev host `bkzk-002.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com`, path `ocapi`, `:213-216` | exact |
| Einstein `config/default.js:140-148`, host `api.cquotient.com` | exact (config value is `https://api.cquotient.com`) |
| SCAPI host constant across tiers; OCAPI host changes per tier (Dev `bkzk-002.dx…`, Prod `production-ap01-zimmermann.demandware.net`) | `config/dev.js`,`test.js`,`sit.js`,`staging.js`,`uat.js`,`production.js` all confirm |
| `npm run env -- <tier>` → `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`; `push:<tier>` → `pwa-kit-dev push -t <target>` | `package.json` scripts + file exists |
| pwa-kit-runtime / pwa-kit-react-sdk **3.18.0**, commerce-sdk-react **5.2.0**, retail-react-app **10.0.0** | node_modules confirms all four |
| SCAPI endpoint table (3.1.1) — all 7 path roots + verbs | matches `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` §4 exactly |
| `useProductSearch` query: `refine:['cgid=…','htype=master']`, `expand:['promotions','variations','prices','images','custom_properties']`, `perPricebook:true`, `allVariationProperties:true` | `overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:52-58` exact |
| `useProduct` also consumed | `productHero.tsx:16`, `hotspotPopup.tsx:12` |
| SLAS private client — `useSLASPrivateClient: true` | `overrides/app/ssr.js:52` |
| CommerceApiProvider wiring; `enablePWAKitPrivateClient`, `privateClientProxyEndpoint` | `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx:132,147,148` |
| NO `mulesoft` entry in any `config/*.js` | `grep -rin mulesoft config/` returns nothing |
| undici connection pool exists | `overrides/app/ssr/connectionPools.ts:42-46` (`mulesoftPool`) |
| MuleSoft direct-read path = orders/returns/boutique-stock/GiveX ONLY, NOT product/pricing | `.docs/integration/03-mulesoft.md` §1 (product/price feed explicitly out of scope) |
| Catalogue/data tooling NOT in `zimmermann-pwa` | no `data/` dir, no `dw.json`, no `data:import` script |
| Instance IDs: shortCode `qmyt7hks`, org `f_ecom_bkzk_002`, siteId `ZimmermannAU` | `.env.sample:71,73`, `.env.dev:6` confirm |

**INACCURATE:**
- **"nine sites total"** (line 80). `config/sites.js` (via `sites.overlay.js`) produces **10 PWA sites** backed by **7 distinct SFCC sites**. Node check: `PWA sites: 10, distinct SFCC: 7`. The "9" appears to count `siteAliases` in `default.js` (which omits AU, the aliasless default). Neither 9.

**UNVERIFIABLE-FROM-CODE (Confluence/TSD-sourced — not errors, but flagged where risky):**
- Catalogue IDs `zimmermann-catalog` / `zimmermann-au-storefront-catalog` (lines 121, 167) — see SHOULD-FIX #2 below.
- `zimmermann-sfccworkplace` cartridge repo (line 166).
- TanStack stale-times 60/30/0s (line 99) — sourced from `01-sfcc.md` §6, not code (code default `staleTime` is 10s in `_app-config`).
- MuleSoft rate-limit open item, MRT env-var rotation, permanent-feed delivery mechanism — all correctly attributed to Confluence.

---

## Part B — Prioritized findings

### BLOCKER
None. The technical core (SCAPI-through-MRT is the real product/price/category path; the blocker is empty data not a missing API; MuleSoft does not feed product/price to the PWA) is accurate and well-supported by code and the integration docs.

### SHOULD-FIX

**1. Wrong site count.** Line 80: "nine sites total, see `config/sites.js`". Correct to **10 PWA storefront sites (backed by 7 SFCC sites; the 4 EU-domestic sites share SFCC `ZimmermannEU`)**. As written it's directly contradicted by the file it cites.

**2. Catalogue IDs asserted as fact but unverifiable and inconsistent with the repo.** Lines 121 and 167 state the master catalogue is `zimmermann-catalog` and the AU storefront catalogue is `zimmermann-au-storefront-catalog`, presented in the "Recommended actions" as a concrete BM step with no TBC marker. These strings appear **nowhere else in the repo**. The only real catalogue ID in the codebase is `"storefront-catalog-eu"` (`.docs/vendor/mulesoft.md:102`, also flagged in `03-mulesoft.md` §9). A squad engineer configuring BM off these invented IDs would be misdirected. Mark them as assumed/to-be-confirmed, or align to the real `storefront-catalog-*` convention and verify with M. Ramachandran.

**3. Writing-convention violation: em/en dashes.** The doc contains **18 em dashes (U+2014)** and **1 en dash (U+2013)** — e.g. the H1 title (line 1), section headings (39, 128, 142, 151), TL;DR/diagram (49), DoD table (178-183), and the Confluence source list (line 211, which also holds the lone en dash: "Build and Deployment Process – Headless Architecture"). This violates the stated no-dash convention. Note for context: the surrounding `zimmermann-pwa` integration docs use em dashes pervasively too, so either the convention applies repo-wide (large cleanup) or not at all — worth a ruling before publishing to Confluence.

### NICE-TO-HAVE

**4. OCAPI framing overclaims current state.** §3.1.5/§3.1.8: OCAPI is described as a live "fallback" reached via `/mobify/proxy/ocapi` "with OCAPI credentials held server-side," and as the catalogue-import channel. In reality OCAPI is **not consumed anywhere in app code** (only referenced in `scripts/switchEnv.mjs` host-validation and sync scripts) — no OCAPI calls, no credential-injection scaffolding. Also, catalogue import via the OCAPI Data API is an **admin/Account-Manager channel**, not the shopper-facing storefront proxy; grouping it under "reached at `/mobify/proxy/ocapi`" conflates two different auth paths. An SFCC expert would notice. Recommend: state OCAPI is configured-but-unused, and separate the admin Data API import channel from the storefront proxy.

**5. "shopper-promotions … wired and proven in the codebase" is overstated.** TL;DR item 2 / line 19. Promotions are only demonstrated via `expand:['promotions']` on `useProductSearch`; there is **no standalone shopper-promotions hook in `overrides/`** (only `useProduct`/`useProductSearch` are used). The standalone promotions capability is inherited from the base `retail-react-app` template, not "proven" in this repo. Soften to reflect that.

**6. `shopper-orders` "lookup" is ambiguous / potentially misleading.** §3.1.1 table row lists shopper-orders as "Order placement and **lookup**". Order **history and detail come from MuleSoft**, not SCAPI (`01-sfcc.md:17`, DMU-007; `03-mulesoft.md`). The "(SFCC-owned checkouts)" qualifier helps, and §3.1.6 gets it right, but the table row alone could mislead. Clarify that "lookup" means the just-placed SFCC order, not order history.

**7. MuleSoft scaffold mechanism mismatch.** §3.1.6 frames the path as `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/…` "not yet wired into `proxyConfigs`," implying the eventual wiring is a proxyConfig. The actual scaffold is an undici `mulesoftPool` for a **server-side `fetch()` from `ssr.js`** (per the file's own header comment) — a different mechanism than PWA Kit proxyConfigs (which can't inject the `client_id`/`client_secret` headers + session-derived `customer_id` this path needs). Worth noting the two are not the same wiring.

**8. Internal tension on the tooling repo.** Line 166 asserts the seed/conversion tooling "lives in the separate `zimmermann-sfccworkplace` cartridge repo," while Open Question 2 (line 188) asks "who owns" it and whether access is possible. Asserting a specific repo name as fact while simultaneously listing it as an open question is contradictory — soften line 166 to "assumed to live in…".

**9. Appendix A package provenance.** The three `@salesforce/*` runtime/SDK packages listed are **transitive** (only `@salesforce/retail-react-app@10.0.0` is a direct dependency in `package.json`); the versions themselves are correct per node_modules. Minor: note they're resolved-transitive, not pinned, so they can drift on a `retail-react-app` bump.

---

## Verdict on the DoD

**The DoD content requirements are substantially met.** All four spike tasks are addressed with correct, code-backed substance:
- Task 1 (inventory: endpoints/payload/auth/data) — accurate; every code citation checked out.
- Task 2 (what serves product/category/pricing in lower envs now) — correct and the "capability exists, data is the blocker" conclusion is well-founded.
- Task 3 (gaps for MuleSoft) — reasonable and honest about open items.
- Task 4 (permanent vs workaround) — defensible classification.

The document is genuinely **sufficient to unblock front-end development** (the SDK/hook path is proven and needs no code change once data exists). It is **only partially sufficient to unblock BM configuration**: the specific BM values a configurator needs (catalogue IDs, pricebook assignments) are **assumed/unverified and in one case contradicted by the repo's own sample data** (SHOULD-FIX #2), and the sandbox's current data state is still an open question. Before publishing to Confluence: fix the site count (#1), mark or correct the catalogue IDs (#2), resolve the dash convention (#3), and soften the OCAPI/promotions overstatements (#4, #5). None of these undermine the central, correct thesis of the spike.
