| Related | SFCC-121 (Validate MuleSoft Sync), SFCC-123 (Contentful design), SFCC-1 (Platform Setup & Environments, owner: M. Ramachandran) |
| Status of this doc | Draft for squad review |
| Last updated | 2026-07-22 |

---

## TL;DR

1. **"MRT" is the hosting and proxy layer, not an API.** Managed Runtime is the PWA Kit Node server. The APIs the storefront actually consumes for product, category, and pricing data are **SCAPI (Salesforce Commerce API, the Shopper APIs)**, reached *through* the MRT proxy.
2. **SCAPI can already serve product, category, and pricing today.** The capability exists now: `shopper-products`, `shopper-search`, and pricebook-aware pricing are wired and proven in this codebase. Standalone `shopper-promotions` is available through the base template and is demonstrated here via `expand=promotions`.
3. **The blocker is empty data, not a missing API.** Product and price data are absent from the lower environments because the source-to-SFCC data feeds have not been built yet: product/catalogue is AP21 to MuleSoft to SFCC, and price is AP21 to SFCC via XML pricebook import (mechanism, SFTP / API / MuleSoft, still to be confirmed). That is a data-population problem, owned server-side, not an MRT or SCAPI capability gap.
4. **MuleSoft does not serve product or pricing to the PWA.** The direct PWA to MRT to MuleSoft path is only for orders, returns, and real-time boutique stock. Product and price master data is a separate server-to-server import into SFCC.
5. **To unblock lower-environment build and test now:** load catalogue and pricebook data into the `bkzk-002` sandbox (Business Manager or the OCAPI Data API), confirm the BM site, catalogue, and pricebook assignment, then the PWA consumes it via SCAPI with no code change.

---

## 1. Objective

Document the SFCC MRT (Managed Runtime) APIs relevant to the Zimmermann storefront build, so the squad has a clear picture of what is available for product, pricing, and category data consumption before MuleSoft is ready. This lets the squad determine what can be built and tested in lower environments in the meantime.

## 2. Background

- Base Business Manager configuration is in place on the SFCC sandbox, but product and price data are currently missing because MuleSoft is not yet ready.
- Understanding the MRT API capabilities tells the squad what can be built and tested in lower environments while that feed is being built.
- A session is to be set up with M. Ramachandran (owner of SFCC-1, Platform Setup & Environments) to confirm the sandbox data-loading approach.
- The storefront is a PWA Kit application (`zimmermann-pwa`) hosted on Managed Runtime, template-extending `@salesforce/retail-react-app`, consuming commerce data from SFCC and editorial content from Contentful.

## 3. Tasks and findings

### 3.1 Task 1: Review and document the available MRT APIs

**How commerce data reaches the storefront.** The browser talks to SFCC through a proxy hosted by Managed Runtime. Nothing calls SFCC directly from a hard-coded backend host; every call goes through an MRT proxy path, which lets MRT attach server-only credentials and keeps secrets out of the browser bundle.

```
Browser (React, SSR + CSR)
   |  @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react (TanStack Query under the hood)
   v
MRT proxy  /mobify/proxy/api    -->  SCAPI  (Shopper APIs): product, category, price, search, promotions, basket, orders, customers
           /mobify/proxy/ocapi  -->  OCAPI  (configured; fallback for gaps; not currently called from app code)
           /mobify/proxy/mulesoft --> MuleSoft (orders, returns, boutique stock ONLY; designed, not yet wired)
   v
SFCC realm (sandbox bkzk-002 in Dev)
```

The single SDK `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (v5.2.0) handles every SFCC call: SLAS token lifecycle, retry, and TanStack Query caching. Verified in `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx` (CommerceApiProvider wiring) and consumed via hooks such as `useProduct` and `useProductSearch`.

#### 3.1.1 SCAPI Shopper APIs (primary path for product, category, pricing)

Reached at MRT proxy path `/mobify/proxy/api` (`config/default.js:131`). These are the APIs that serve the data this spike is about.

| API family | Path root | Serves | Verbs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shopper Products | `/product/shopper-products/v1/*` | Product detail, master/variant resolution, images, prices on the product | GET |
| Shopper Search | `/search/shopper-search/v1/*` | Category product listing (`cgid` refinement), keyword search, faceting, sort, suggestions | GET |
| Shopper Promotions | `/pricing/shopper-promotions/v1/*` | Active promotions, coupon validation | GET |
| Shopper Login (SLAS) | `/checkout/shopper-login/oauth2/*` | Guest and registered auth, token lifecycle | GET, POST |
| Shopper Baskets | `/checkout/shopper-baskets/v2/*` | Basket / cart lifecycle, line items | GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE |
| Shopper Orders | `/checkout/shopper-orders/v1/*` | Order placement and lookup of the just-placed order (SFCC-owned checkouts). Order history and detail come from MuleSoft, not SCAPI (see 3.1.6) | POST, GET |
| Shopper Customers | `/customer/shopper-customers/v1/*` | Profile, addresses, saved-payment references | GET, POST, PATCH |

Source: `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` section 4.

**Pricing is fully supported through SCAPI.** The canonical query in the codebase (`overrides/app/pages/home/index.tsx:52-58`) uses `useProductSearch` with `refine: ['cgid=<categoryId>', 'htype=master']` and `expand: ['promotions','variations','prices','images','custom_properties']`, `perPricebook: true`, `allVariationProperties: true`. This demonstrates category refinement plus pricebook-aware pricing and promotion expansion working end to end, given data exists.

#### 3.1.2 Endpoint structure, base URL, and environments

- **SCAPI base host:** `{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`, proxied via `/mobify/proxy/api`. Verified: `config/default.js:210` host `qmyt7hks.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`.
- **Instance identifiers** (non-secret; injected from env into the SDK provider at `config/default.js:132-137`):
  - `shortCode`: `qmyt7hks`
  - `organizationId`: `f_ecom_bkzk_002` (realm/instance `bkzk_002`)
  - `siteId`: `ZimmermannAU` (default). The app defines 10 PWA storefront sites backed by 7 distinct SFCC sites (the four EU-domestic locales share SFCC site `ZimmermannEU`); see `config/sites.overlay.js`.
  - `clientId`: SLAS client ID (public identifier, held in `COMMERCE_API_CLIENT_ID`)
- **Per-environment config:** `config/dev.js`, `test.js`, `sit.js`, `staging.js`, `uat.js`, `production.js` each override `proxyConfigs`. The SCAPI host stays constant (`qmyt7hks...`); the OCAPI host changes per tier (Dev to `bkzk-002.dx...`, Prod to `production-ap01-zimmermann.demandware.net`).
- **Env switching:** `npm run env -- <tier>` (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`); deploy per tier via `npm run push:<tier>`, which runs `pwa-kit-dev push -t <target>`.
- MRT environment variables are managed per environment in the Managed Runtime console and rotated independently of the codebase (Confluence: Technical Solution Design, PWA).

#### 3.1.3 Authentication

- **SLAS private-client flow** issues a guest access token (anonymous shopper, refreshed silently) and a registered shopper token (after email/password login). Tokens are JWTs carrying customer ID, unique shopper ID (USID), and a refresh token.
- **Secrets stay server-side.** The SLAS client secret is an MRT environment variable and never reaches the browser; the authorisation-code exchange is proxied through the MRT private-client endpoint. The SLAS client ID and SCAPI short code remain in the bundle as public identifiers. Confirmed in `overrides/app/ssr.js:52` (`useSLASPrivateClient: true`) and `overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx:132,147-148`.
- **Refresh tokens** live in `httpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Strict` cookies set by the SSR layer; browser JavaScript never sees the raw refresh token.
- **Multi-site tokens are channel-scoped.** A token for one site is not valid for another; a storefront switch triggers a fresh server-side authorisation (SLAS Trusted System on Behalf).

Source: `.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` section 3.

#### 3.1.4 Payload format and query conventions

- **Format:** JSON over HTTPS (TLS 1.2+), standard SCAPI response envelopes.
- **Every request carries** site ID, organisation ID, locale, currency, and the SLAS bearer token.
- **Efficiency levers used:** `expand=` to pull promotions/variations/prices/images in one call; `fields=` projection to trim payloads; `perPricebook: true` for pricebook-aware pricing; TanStack Query dedup and caching (documented working targets: catalogue stale time ~60s, promotions ~30s, basket 0s, per `01-sfcc.md` section 6; the app-level default `staleTime` is 10s).

#### 3.1.5 OCAPI (configured proxy; not currently consumed in app code)

- A proxy path `/mobify/proxy/ocapi` is configured (`config/default.js:213-216`, Dev host `bkzk-002.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com`) so that any operation not covered by SCAPI can be proxied through MRT with OCAPI credentials held server-side. No OCAPI credentials ever reach the browser.
- Current state: OCAPI is **not called from application code**; it is referenced only in host-validation and sync tooling (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`, `scripts/sfcc/*.mjs`). It is a configured capability held in reserve, not an active runtime dependency.
- Note the distinction from the import channel below: the **admin OCAPI Data API** used to load catalogue data (3.1.8) is a separate, admin-authenticated channel, not the shopper-facing `/mobify/proxy/ocapi` storefront proxy.

#### 3.1.6 MuleSoft-direct reads via MRT (not product, category, or pricing)

There is a designed direct path `PWA to MRT to MuleSoft` at `/mobify/proxy/mulesoft/...` for a small set of reads where SFCC adds nothing to the round-trip. It is **scaffolded but not yet wired**: no `mulesoft` entry exists in any `config/*.js`, and the intended mechanism is a server-side `fetch()` from `ssr.js` over a dedicated undici connection pool (`overrides/app/ssr/connectionPools.ts:42-46`, `mulesoftPool`), not a PWA Kit `proxyConfig`. A plain proxyConfig would not suffice, because this path must inject `client_id`/`client_secret` request headers and a session-derived `customer_id` that proxyConfigs cannot add.

In scope for this path: order history list, order detail, returns, real-time boutique stock (Find in Boutique / BOPIS), GiveX balance check. **Product, category, and pricing are explicitly out of scope for this path.** Source: `.docs/integration/03-mulesoft.md`.

#### 3.1.7 Einstein recommendations (adjacent capability)

Personalised recommendations use the Einstein API (`config/default.js:140-148`, host `https://api.cquotient.com`), consent-gated, with a static SFCC merchandising-group fallback. Not part of the core product/category/pricing consumption but available through the same app.

#### 3.1.8 Catalogue and pricebook population path (server-to-server, the missing piece)

This is what "MuleSoft is not yet ready" refers to, and it is not an MRT capability at all:

- **Product:** AP21 (ERP, system of record) to MuleSoft (transform to SFCC Catalog XML) to SFCC, delivered via the **admin OCAPI Data API** (`/s/-/dw/data/v*/catalogs`) or SFTP + import job. Per the Confluence TSD, a master catalogue plus per-site storefront catalogues.
- **Price:** AP21 to SFCC pricebooks, per-site and per-currency, loaded as SFCC Pricebook XML (`pricebook.xsd`). Per the TSD, **there is no direct MuleSoft price integration today**; the delivery mechanism (SFTP / API / MuleSoft) is still to be confirmed (TSD Price open item 1). Pricebook IDs follow `{site}-{currency}-list-prices` and `{site}-{currency}-sale-prices` (e.g. `au-aud-list-prices`, `au-aud-sale-prices`; sale pricebook parents the list pricebook). Import via `sfcc-ci instance:import` or Business Manager Site Import.
- Product IDs (per TSD): master = `stylecode` (e.g. `4673TS251`); variant = `stylecode + colourcode + sizecode`.
- The master-catalogue-to-storefront-category assignment is set in Business Manager and cannot be set via XML import.
- **Catalogue ID caveat:** the TSD names the master as `zimmermann-catalog` and storefront catalogues as `zimmermann-<site>-storefront-catalog`. The PWA repo does not contain SFCC catalogue configuration (that lives in the SFCC cartridge repo), so these IDs are expected to be absent here; that absence is not a contradiction. The only similar-looking value in the repo, `storefront-catalog-eu`, is the `shop.id` field inside a sample MuleSoft order-response payload (`.docs/vendor/mulesoft.md`), not an SFCC catalogue definition. Confirm the actual sandbox catalogue IDs with M. Ramachandran before using them for BM configuration.

Source: Confluence "TSD: Product, SFCC Catalogue & Data Integration" and "TSD: Price, SFCC Pricebooks & Global-e".

### 3.2 Task 2: Which MRT APIs can serve product, category, and pricing in lower environments now

**Answer: SCAPI can, as soon as data exists in the sandbox.** The API capability is not the constraint. `shopper-products`, `shopper-search` (with `cgid` category refinement), and pricebook-aware pricing via `expand=prices` with `perPricebook=true` all work against any populated SFCC instance.

The only thing missing in the lower environments is **data in the SFCC catalogue and pricebooks**. Once data is loaded (see section 4), front-end development and testing can proceed against SCAPI with no dependency on the upstream data feeds being finished.

| Capability | Available in lower env now? | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| Product detail (`shopper-products`) | Yes, once catalogue data is loaded | Sandbox catalogue populated |
| Category listing / search (`shopper-search`, `cgid`) | Yes, once catalogue + storefront categories + search index exist | BM catalogue assignment + search index rebuild |
| Pricing (`prices`, `perPricebook`) | Yes, once pricebooks are loaded and assigned | Sandbox pricebooks populated + assigned to site |
| Promotions (`shopper-promotions`) | Yes, once promotions are configured in BM | BM promotion setup |
| Auth (SLAS) | Yes, working now | SLAS client already configured |

### 3.3 Task 3: Limitations and gaps to be covered by MuleSoft (or elsewhere)

- **No catalogue or price data in the sandbox** until either sample/manual data is loaded or the source-to-SFCC product and price feeds are built (dependency: SFCC-121).
- **Catalogue/price freshness and delta handling** (event vs scheduled, sale-price removal signals) are data-feed concerns, not SCAPI concerns.
- **MuleSoft real-time rate limits** for the direct-read path are unconfirmed (Confluence "MuleSoft Integration, Open Questions", item G3).
- **Delivery mechanism for catalogue import** (OCAPI Data API vs SFTP + import job) and the feed trigger are still open (Confluence TSD Product, open item 1).
- **Per-environment SLAS client ID / short code** for non-Dev tiers partly outstanding (`.docs/integration/01-sfcc.md` section 7).
- The **MuleSoft direct-read path** (`/mobify/proxy/mulesoft`) is not yet wired, so order history, returns, and boutique stock are not consumable from the PWA until it is added and MuleSoft endpoints are provisioned per environment.

### 3.4 Task 4: Permanent architecture vs current-state workaround

| Element | Classification | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| SCAPI via MRT proxy for product / category / pricing consumption | **Permanent** | The storefront's supported model for all shopper data |
| SLAS private-client auth via MRT | **Permanent** | Standard PWA Kit pattern |
| AP21 to MuleSoft to SFCC product/catalogue feed (population) | **Permanent** | The intended catalogue data source; not yet built |
| AP21 to SFCC price feed via pricebook XML import (population) | **Permanent** | No direct MuleSoft price integration per TSD; mechanism (SFTP / API / MuleSoft) to be confirmed; not yet built |
| OCAPI via MRT for operations SCAPI does not cover | **Permanent (semi)** | Configured fallback by design; currently unused; shrinks as SCAPI coverage grows |
| PWA to MRT to MuleSoft direct reads (orders, returns, boutique stock) | **Permanent** | Designed, not yet wired |
| Manual / sample catalogue and pricebook load into the sandbox | **Workaround** | Current-state only, to unblock lower-env build and test before the permanent product and price feeds exist |

## 4. Recommended actions to unblock lower environments

1. **Load catalogue and pricebook data into the `bkzk-002` sandbox.** Options, in order of preference for a quick unblock:
   - Import a sample/seed catalogue via the **admin OCAPI Data API** (`/s/-/dw/data/v*/catalogs`) or a site-archive import job in Business Manager.
   - Load pricebooks as SFCC Pricebook XML via `sfcc-ci instance:import` or Business Manager Site Import; IDs follow `{site}-{currency}-list-prices` / `-sale-prices` (e.g. `au-aud-list-prices`).
   - Note: the catalogue/data tooling and sample data are **not in `zimmermann-pwa`** (the PWA repo only consumes). Per the TSD, the conversion/seed tooling is assumed to live in a separate SFCC cartridge repo (referred to as `zimmermann-sfccworkplace`); confirm the repo name, ownership, and access with M. Ramachandran.
2. **Confirm Business Manager configuration** on the sandbox: site catalogue assignment (catalogue IDs to be confirmed against the sandbox, see the caveat in 3.1.8), storefront category tree, pricebook assignment per site/currency, and a search index rebuild so `shopper-search` returns results.
3. **Verify SCAPI reachability** from the sandbox with a SLAS guest token and a `shopper-search` smoke test, to confirm data is queryable before front-end work starts.
4. **Front-end proceeds via `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`** hooks against the populated sandbox: no code change is needed once data exists.
5. **Track the permanent feeds** (SFCC-121) separately; the workaround load is throwaway once the permanent product and price feeds are delivering.

## 5. Definition of Done: status

> **DoD:** A documented inventory of relevant MRT APIs is produced and shared with the squad, sufficient to unblock BM configuration and front-end development in lower environments.

| DoD element | Status |
|---|---|
| Inventory of relevant MRT/SCAPI APIs (endpoints, structure, payload, auth, data) | Done, section 3.1 |
| Assessment of what can serve product/category/pricing in lower envs | Done, section 3.2 |
| Limitations and gaps for MuleSoft to cover | Done, section 3.3 |
| Permanent vs workaround classification | Done, section 3.4 |
| Actions sufficient to unblock front-end dev | Done, section 4 (proven SDK/hook path; no code change once data exists) |
| Actions sufficient to unblock BM config | Partial, section 4; the exact catalogue IDs and current sandbox data state are open questions for M. Ramachandran (section 6) |
| Shared with the squad | Pending: this draft to be reviewed, then published to Confluence |

## 6. Open questions (for M. Ramachandran / integration team)

1. What product / category / price data (if any) is currently loaded in the `bkzk-002` sandbox, and how did it get there?
2. What are the actual catalogue IDs on the sandbox (master and per-site storefront)? The TSD names them `zimmermann-catalog` and `zimmermann-<site>-storefront-catalog`; please confirm these are correct for the sandbox.
3. Who owns the SFCC cartridge repo and the sample/seed catalogue data, and can we get access to run an import?
4. Preferred sandbox load mechanism for the interim: OCAPI Data API, BM site-archive import, or manual BM entry?
5. Is the base BM config (site catalogue assignment, pricebook assignment, search index) already complete on the sandbox, or is any of it outstanding?
6. Confirmed delivery mechanism and trigger for the permanent AP21 to MuleSoft to SFCC catalogue and price feed (ties to SFCC-121).

## Appendix A: Config reference (verified in code)

| Item | Value / location |
|---|---|
| PWA Kit runtime | `@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime` / `-react-sdk` 3.18.0 (transitive via the base template) |
| Base template | `@salesforce/retail-react-app` 10.0.0 (direct devDependency; template extensibility, `overrides/`) |
| Commerce SDK | `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` 5.2.0 (transitive) |
| Commerce API params | `config/default.js:130-138` |
| Proxy configs | `config/default.js:208-217` (`api` to SCAPI, `ocapi` to sandbox) |
| SSR / SLAS private client | `overrides/app/ssr.js:52` |
| SCAPI host (Dev) | `qmyt7hks.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com` |
| OCAPI host (Dev) | `bkzk-002.dx.commercecloud.salesforce.com` |
| Org / site (Dev) | `f_ecom_bkzk_002` / `ZimmermannAU` |
| Sites | 10 PWA sites, 7 distinct SFCC sites (`config/sites.overlay.js`) |
| Secrets | Held as MRT env vars / local `.env` (gitignored); never in the browser bundle |

Note: the three `@salesforce/*` runtime and SDK packages are resolved transitively through `@salesforce/retail-react-app`; only the base template is pinned as a direct devDependency, so those versions can move on a template bump.

Objective: document the MRT (Managed Runtime) APIs available for product, category, and pricing so the squad knows what can be built/tested in lower environments while MuleSoft is not yet ready. Background note: "Angelo (=Marcel) to set up session with Mani." Mani = Manikandan Ramachandran (owns SFCC-1 Platform Setup & Environments epic).

**Crux finding (the reframe the spike needs):** MRT is the PWA Kit hosting/proxy layer, not an API. Product/category/pricing reach the PWA via **SCAPI Shopper APIs** (shopper-products v1, shopper-search v1, shopper-promotions v1) proxied through MRT (`/mobify/proxy/api`, shortCode `qmyt7hks`), using `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` v5.2.0 hooks with SLAS private-client auth. OCAPI is a proxied fallback (`/mobify/proxy/ocapi`, dev sandbox `bkzk-002`). MuleSoft does NOT serve product/price to the PWA — its role there is the server-to-server AP21→MuleSoft→SFCC catalogue import (OCAPI Data API or SFTP). Price is separate: AP21→SFCC via pricebook XML import (sfcc-ci / BM Site Import), and per TSD Price (292388871) there is NO direct MuleSoft price integration; mechanism (SFTP/API/MuleSoft) is TBC. Pricebook IDs: `{site}-{currency}-list-prices`/`-sale-prices` (e.g. `au-aud-list-prices`). So SCAPI is fully capable NOW; the real blocker is that SFCC has no catalog/price data yet because that MuleSoft feed isn't built.

**Unblock lower envs:** load catalog + pricebook data into the SFCC sandbox via BM or OCAPI Data API so the PWA can consume via SCAPI immediately. Sample-catalog tooling (`data/sample/catalogs`, `data:import:sample`) is NOT in zimmermann-pwa — it lives in the separate `zimmermann-sfccworkplace` cartridge repo (per Confluence TSD Product page 292061208). The PWA repo only consumes.

**Permanent vs workaround:** SCAPI-via-MRT (consumption) + MuleSoft catalogue/pricebook feed (population) are permanent. Manual/sample catalog load into sandbox is the temporary workaround. OCAPI fallback is semi-permanent (anything SCAPI doesn't cover).

content.text:
Love this approach. Let's build it up layer by layer. Here's **Phase 1 — ELI5**, deliberately simple; we'll add precision in later phases.

---

## Phase 1: The whole spike, explained simply

Imagine you're building a **shop**. 🛍️

Shoppers come in and want to see **products**: the name, a photo, and the price. But here's the thing, your shop doesn't actually *keep* the products itself. There's a big **storeroom** out the back that holds everything.

Your shop isn't allowed to just wander into the storeroom and grab things. Instead, there's a **helpful waiter** standing at a hatch. You ask the waiter, *"Can I get the red dress, its photo, and its price?"* and the waiter goes into the storeroom, fetches it, and hands it back. That waiter is the only way your shop talks to the storeroom.

**Now the problem:** the storeroom shelves are **empty**. 😟 The delivery trucks that are *supposed* to stock those shelves haven't started running yet. So even though the waiter is ready and willing, there's nothing back there to fetch. Your shop-builders are stuck twiddling their thumbs with nothing to display.

**Your job (the spike) is NOT to build the shop.** It's to be a detective and write a short report answering three simple questions:

1. **What can the waiter actually get us?** (What can we ask for, and how?)
2. **Can we sneak some pretend products onto the shelves ourselves**, so the shop-builders can keep working while we wait for the real trucks?
3. **Which parts of this are the permanent, forever setup, and which are just temporary duct-tape** to get us through the wait?

That's the entire spike in a nutshell: **investigate and document what's possible right now, so nobody is blocked.**

> One-line version: *"The tools to fetch products work fine, the shelves are just empty, so let's document what the tools can do and figure out how to stock the shelves ourselves in the meantime."*

---

That's the big picture. When you're ready, **Phase 2** gets one notch more granular: I'll put real names to the shop, the storeroom, the waiter, and the trucks (SFCC, MRT, SCAPI, MuleSoft, AP21), and explain *why this is a "spike" and not just a task*.

Want me to go to Phase 2?

content.thinking:

I'm mapping out the full data flow: Salesforce Commerce API is the interface the shop uses to request products, MRT acts as the proxy layer that keeps the shop from directly accessing the storeroom, MuleSoft handles the integration between AP21 (the ERP source of truth) and SFCC, and Contentful manages the editorial content separate from product data. The complete chain runs from AP21 through MuleSoft into SFCC, then through the API via MRT to reach the storefront and ultimately the shopper.

Now I'm clarifying a key distinction: people often say "MRT API" colloquially, but MRT is really the hosting counter while SCAPI is the actual service doing the fetching—I'll introduce this gently in Phase 2 and dig deeper later. A spike here makes sense because it's a time-boxed research task to answer what's actually available through these systems right now given the empty storeroom, so the team can plan real work with confidence instead of guessing.

I'll structure this with a mapping table showing the players and their roles, explain why a spike fits better than a story, touch on the board's spike format (Objective/Background/Tasks/DoD), and then preview Phase 3 where I'll dig into how data actually flows through the two paths and the capability-versus-data distinction.

content.text:
Nice. **Phase 2** — same story, but now with the real names and roles, plus *why this is a "spike."*

---

## Phase 2: Who's who, and why it's a "spike"

### The cast, mapped to Phase 1

| Phase 1 analogy | Real name | What it actually is |
|---|---|---|
| 🛍️ The shop | **The PWA storefront** (`zimmermann-pwa`) | The React website shoppers see. Built on Salesforce's **PWA Kit** framework. Your team's code. |
| 🏬 The storeroom | **SFCC** (Salesforce Commerce Cloud) | The commerce platform that *holds* and *owns* the real commerce data: products, prices, categories, baskets, orders. The "system of record" for the shop. |
| 🧑‍🍳 The waiter (fetches from the storeroom) | **SCAPI** (Salesforce Commerce API, the "Shopper APIs") | The actual service the shop calls to ask for products, search, prices, etc. This is the real "API." |
| 🏛️ The counter the waiter works from | **MRT** (Managed Runtime) | The server that *hosts* your shop and safely passes its requests through to the waiter. The shop never talks to the storeroom directly; everything goes via MRT. |
| 🚚 The delivery trucks | **MuleSoft** | The "integration middleware" that moves goods into the storeroom from head office. Not ready yet, which is the whole problem. |
| 🏢 Head office (where products truly originate) | **AP21** | The brand's ERP (their master inventory/pricing system). The true source of product and price data. |
| 🖼️ The window dressing / posters | **Contentful** | The CMS for editorial content (banners, lookbook copy). Styles the shop, but does **not** hold products. |

**The full chain:** AP21 (head office) → MuleSoft (trucks) → SFCC (storeroom) → SCAPI (waiter) through MRT (the counter) → your PWA (the shop) → shopper. 👀

### The one subtlety worth planting now
The ticket is called *"Document SFCC **MRT** API Capabilities."* But notice: **MRT is the counter, not the waiter.** The thing that actually fetches data is **SCAPI**. People say "MRT API" loosely to mean "the stuff we can reach through Managed Runtime." Part of what your spike does is quietly clear that up, the real answer is *"it's SCAPI, reached through MRT."* (We'll dig into exactly how in Phase 3.)

### Why this is a "spike" and not a normal task

A **spike** is a **time-boxed investigation whose deliverable is knowledge, not a feature.** In Scrum, when there's too much uncertainty to safely estimate or start building, you first do a spike to *reduce the unknowns*.

- A normal **Story** would be: *"Build the product listing page."* → ships working code.
- Your **Spike** is: *"Find out what we can even build against right now, and how."* → ships a **document** (the one we drafted).

Why a spike fits *here*: with the storeroom empty and MuleSoft not running, nobody's certain what's actually usable today. Rather than have the team guess and possibly waste effort, one person (you) investigates and writes it down so everyone can plan with confidence. That's why the "Definition of Done" is *"a documented inventory... shared with the squad"*, the output is understanding, captured on paper.

That's also why the ticket follows the board's spike shape: **Objective / Background / Tasks / Definition of Done**, a research brief, not a build ticket.

### How your three ELI5 questions became the spike's four tasks
- *"What can the waiter get us?"* → **Task 1** (document the available APIs).
- *"Can we stock the shelves ourselves in the meantime?"* → **Task 2** (what can serve data in lower environments now).
- *(the gap between)* → **Task 3** (limitations MuleSoft still needs to cover).
- *"What's permanent vs duct-tape?"* → **Task 4** (permanent architecture vs workaround).

---

**Phase 3** goes a notch deeper: the *two different data paths* (asking for data vs. filling the shelves), and the single most important insight in the whole spike, why "the API works but the data is missing" is a completely different problem than "the API doesn't work." Ready for Phase 3?

content.text:
Here's **Phase 3** — the mechanics, and the one insight everything hinges on.

---

## Phase 3: Two directions of data, and why "empty" ≠ "broken"

### There are two completely separate journeys data makes

Everyone pictures "the shop shows products" as one thing. It's actually **two independent flows moving in opposite directions**, run by different teams, with different technology.

**① Reading data OUT (consumption)** — the waiter fetching for a shopper:

```
Shopper → PWA → MRT proxy (/mobify/proxy/api) → SCAPI → SFCC storeroom → back out as JSON
```

This is what happens live, on every page view. In real terms:
- Your React code calls a hook like `useProductSearch(...)`.
- That fires a request to `/mobify/proxy/api/...` on your own MRT server.
- **MRT forwards it** to the SCAPI host (`qmyt7hks.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`), attaching the secret credentials so the browser never sees them.
- SCAPI reads from SFCC and returns the product as JSON.
- (First, the shop quietly got a **guest token** via **SLAS**, think of it as a wristband proving it's an allowed visitor. No wristband, no service.)

**This flow is fully built and working today.** ✅

**② Getting data IN (population)** — filling the shelves:

```
AP21 (head office) → MuleSoft (trucks) → SFCC storeroom     ← products / categories
AP21 → SFCC pricebook import                                 ← prices
```

This is **server-to-server**, invisible to the browser, and runs on a schedule. It's how the storeroom gets stocked in the first place.

**This flow is NOT built yet.** 🚧 That's the blocker.

```
        POPULATION (in)                          CONSUMPTION (out)
  AP21 ──trucks(MuleSoft)──▶ SFCC ◀──asks(SCAPI via MRT)── PWA ──▶ shopper
        [NOT built yet]      (empty)   [built & working]
```

### The insight the whole spike turns on

To a shopper, two very different problems look **identical** ("no products on the page"):

| What it looks like | What's actually wrong | Who fixes it | The fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| No products show | 🅐 The **waiter/counter is broken** (SCAPI/MRT can't do the job) | Front-end + platform | Code / config work |
| No products show | 🅑 The **waiter works, shelves are empty** (no data in SFCC) | Integration / data team | Load data. No code. |

**The spike's central finding is that it's 100% 🅑, not 🅐.** SCAPI-through-MRT is fully capable right now. Nothing is broken. The storeroom is just empty because the trucks (MuleSoft) haven't run.

### Why that distinction is a big deal

1. **It reassigns the problem.** It's *not* a front-end bug and *not* an API limitation. It's a data-pipeline gap owned server-side. Your team is not the blocker.
2. **It changes the fix entirely.** You don't write code or file an API ticket, you get *data* into the storeroom.
3. **And here's the unlock:** the waiter doesn't care *how* the products got onto the shelves. So you can **hand-stock the shelves yourself**, load a sample catalogue and sample pricebooks straight into the sandbox, and the shop-builders can start immediately, *in parallel* with waiting for the real trucks. That single realisation is what turns "we're blocked" into "we're not blocked."

### A wrinkle to file away (we'll open it fully in Phase 4)
MuleSoft actually wears **two different hats**, which is a big source of confusion:
- **Hat 1 (the trucks):** server-to-server, filling the storeroom with product/catalogue data. *Not for the browser.*
- **Hat 2 (a tiny side-door):** a *separate*, direct `PWA → MRT → MuleSoft` path for a few live reads like order history and boutique stock. *Not products or prices.*

People conflate these, which muddies the "is MuleSoft involved?" question. The spike keeps them clearly separate.

---

**Phase 4** gets concrete and specific: we walk through the actual document, the real API endpoints in the inventory, the exact "permanent vs duct-tape" verdicts, the step-by-step "how to stock the shelves" plan, and the genuine gotchas we caught during validation (price might not even use MuleSoft; the catalogue-ID caveat; OCAPI sitting in reserve). Ready for Phase 4?

1	# Managed Runtime Overview
2	
3	[Managed Runtime](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html) provides the infrastructure to deploy, host, and monitor your PWA Kit storefront.
4	
5	:::important
6	Managed Runtime only supports applications created from a PWA Kit template. The source code for the available templates can be found in the `template-*` folders in the [PWA Kit repository](https://github.com/SalesforceCommerceCloud/pwa-kit/tree/develop/packages) on GitHub.
7	:::
8	
9	This guide covers the main parts of Managed Runtime and how to access it.
10	
11	::include{src="../../shared/managed-runtime-access.md"}
12	
13	:::important
14	Before you can use Managed Runtime and Runtime Admin, ask your B2C Commerce administrator to add one of these roles to your account in Account Manager: **Managed Runtime User** or **Managed Runtime Admin**.
15	:::
16	
17	## Environments
18	
19	An **environment** is the term used to describe all of the cloud infrastructure and configuration values for a particular storefront hosted by Managed Runtime. Environments are used to separate your production storefront from other storefronts that are deployed for other purposes, such as development or testing.
20	
21	:::note
22	In the [Managed Runtime API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=Summary), environments are called “targets,” but both terms refer to the same thing.
23	:::
24	
25	Because environments run on highly efficient microservices that automatically scale up and down, you can create as many environments as you need at no additional cost. For example, you could create a short-lived environment dedicated to a single agile development sprint or for a single user story within that sprint. When you no longer need an environment, we encourage you to delete them.
26	
27	### Production Environments
28	
29	Environments marked as production are prioritized for monitoring by Salesforce’s Support team. For production environments, you can also [Debug Using Log Center](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/debugging.html#debug-using-log-center). To mark an environment as a production, you have two choices:
30	
31	1. Use the Runtime Admin tool. Step-by-step instructions for creating an environment or editing an existing environment are found in the [Environments](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html#environments) section of the Administration guide.
32	2. Use the Managed Runtime API. The [projects_target_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_create) and [projects_target_partial_update](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_partial_update) endpoints both feature the `is_production` parameter. To mark an environment as production with these endpoints, set `is_production` to `true`.
33	
34	:::important
35	By default, you can mark up to 10 environments as production. To increase your limit, contact Support.
36	:::
37	
38	## Bundles
39	
40	The storefront code that runs on an environment is called a **bundle**. Use the developer tools included in PWA Kit to generate a bundle and push it to Managed Runtime.
41	
42	:::note
43	A bundle is a snapshot of your code at a specific point in time. It’s *immutable*: After a bundle has been created, it can’t be changed. Having this complete and accurate history of bundles makes troubleshooting deployments easier.
44	:::
45	
46	After pushing the bundle, you can use the Runtime Admin or Managed Runtime API to designate that bundle as “deployed.” Each project can have multiple bundles, but each environment can have only one bundle that's designated as deployed. You can change which bundle is designated as deployed at any time. For more information, see [Push and Deploy Bundles](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/pushing-and-deploying-bundles.html).
47	
48	## Projects and Organizations
49	
50	To help you manage multiple environments, each environment also belongs to a **project** and each project belongs to an **organization**. An organization can contain multiple projects for multiple storefronts and each project can contain multiple environments. A Managed Runtime user can belong to multiple organizations to separate different work streams.
51	
52	Each organization can have a maximum of 100 total environments and a maximum of 10 production environments. If you need to raise these limits, contact your Salesforce Support representative.
53	
54	Organizations and user organization membership is determined by settings in Account Manager. A user can belong to an organization as either a member or an admin. 56	:::important
57	To assign a user the admin organization membership, contact Salesforce Support.
58	:::
59

61	
62	All users must be assigned the `Managed Runtime User` or `Managed Runtime Admin` via [Account Manager](https://account.demandware.com) for accessing Managed Runtime.
63	
64	### Organization Roles and Permissions
65	
66	Any user can have the following capabilities for a Managed Runtime organization:
67	
68	- **Browse:** View all projects for an Organization.
69	- **Certificate:** View or manage TLS Certificates for an organization.

71	### Project Roles and Permissions
72	
73	Any user can have the following capabilities for a Managed Runtime project:
74	
75	- **Browse:** View the project in Runtime Admin.
76	- **Manage Redirects:** Manage redirects for the project. Please review the [Redirects documentation](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html?q=Redirects#redirects) to learn more.
77	- **Deploy:** Deploy new bundles or revert the deployment to an older bundle.

79	- **Access Logs:** Tail logs across all environments.
80	- **View and Manage Environment Variables:** See and manage environment variables in each environment. See [Environment Variables](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/environment-variables.html).
81	
82	Each user is assigned a project role that determines which abilities they have. (A user can only have *one* role.) Project roles can be assigned to any user within an organization.
83	
84	The following table shows which abilities are associated with each project role:
85	
86	| Project Role | Browse | Manage Redirects | Deploy | Manage Team | Access Logs | View and Manage Environment Variables |
87	| :----------- | :----- | :--------------- | :----- | :---------- | :---------- | :------------------------------------ |
88	| Admin        | Yes    | Yes              | Yes    | Yes         | Yes         | Yes                                   |
89	| Developer    | Yes    | Yes              | Yes    | No          | Yes         | Yes                                   |
90	| Marketer     | Yes    | Yes              | No     | No          | No          | No                                    |
91	| Viewer       | Yes    | No               | No     | No          | No          | No                                    |

93	## App Server
94	
95	Within each Managed Runtime environment, the [React](https://reactjs.org/) app in the published bundle runs inside a [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) environment. To respond to page requests and render the results, we use the [Express](https://expressjs.com/) web framework with the help of PWA Kit’s [rendering](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/rendering.html) and [routing](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/routing.html) systems. 96	
97	Because PWA Kit’s rendering and routing system handles the differences between local development environments and Managed Runtime environments, your code runs in a predictable way when you deploy it. 98	
99	Currently, the App Server supports Transport Layer Security (TLS) versions 1.2 and greater.

104	
105	- `DEPLOY_TARGET`: ID of the environment.
106	- `EXTERNAL_DOMAIN_NAME`: The domain name set on the environment.

112	
113	- A web application firewall (WAF) to protect your environments from attackers
114	- A proxy server to speed up API requests

125	
126	1. The [Managed Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/), a web-based UI.

138	- Redirects

151	
152	- Environments only respond to requests whose HTTP `Host` header matches their External Hostname set in Runtime Admin.
153	- The path `/` only accepts HTTP GET requests.
154	- Request and response size can’t exceed 6 MB.
155	- The maximum size of the HTTP request line and headers is 10240 bytes. Requests exceeding this size return an [HTTP 413 Content Too Large](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/413).
156	  - Of the 10,240 bytes, 1,500 bytes are reserved for internal use, 1,800 bytes for authorization headers, and 1,000 bytes for Salesforce B2C Commerce API (SCAPI). 5,940 bytes are left for custom request headers, including cookies.
157	- Cookies, including the HTTP request `Cookie` and HTTP response `Set-Cookie` header aren't supported by default. Cookies are supported in PWA Kit version 3.1.0 or greater. See [Personalize with Cookies](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/personalize-with-cookies.html).
158	- Requests with headers that start with `_` are not supported. These requests will be dropped.
159	- HTTP requests originating from Managed Runtime environments don't use fixed IP addresses. To allow list requests from the App Server use the [AWS IP Range](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-ip-ranges.html) for `EC2`. To allow list requests from Proxies, use `CLOUDFRONT_ORIGIN_FACING`.
160	- The path prefix `/mobify` is reserved for managed endpoints. These endpoints include:
161	  - `/mobify/ping`: Returns an HTTP 200 response code when the environment is operating correctly.
162	  - `/mobify/redirect/$path`: Returns a similar response as [projects_target_redirect_retrieve](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_retrieve).
163	  - `/mobify/proxy/$name`: Returns a response from a [proxy](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/proxying-requests.html).
164	- You can bypass the CDN cache using the HTTP request header: `x-mobify-cachebreaker: 1`
165	- Environment IP Allowlists support up to 250 IP addresses. This limit can't be raised.
166	- Environment access control headers support up to 2 headers. Each header:
167	  - Can contain up to 128 characters.
168	  - Can be a combination of alphanumeric characters and - and \_ characters
169	  - See [Access Control Headers](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html#access-control-headers).
170	
171	### Rendering
172	
173	- The execution time for App Server requests is limited to 20 seconds for production environments and 16 seconds for non-production environments. After this time, an HTTP 502 is returned.
174	- Unhandled promise rejections break app rendering.
175	
176	### Deployments
177	
178	- The maximum size for bundles is 400 MB and the maximum size of all `ssr_only` and `ssr_shared` files within the bundle is 249 MB.
179	- Static assets that can be uploaded and served are limited to the following content types: `application/javascript`, `application/json`, `image/png` ,`image/gif`, `image/jpeg`, `image/svg+xml`, `image/webp`, `text/css`, `text/plain` and fonts (`ttf`, `woff`, `woff2`, `otf`, etc). All other content types need to be served by an external system.
180	
181	### Proxies
182	
183	Managed Runtime Proxies have different [constraints](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/proxying-requests.html#constraints).
184	
185	## Availability
186	
187	You can subscribe to updates regarding the availability of Managed Runtime services on [Salesforce Status](https://status.salesforce.com/products/B2C_Commerce_Cloud).
188	
189	## Next Steps
190	
191	Now that you have an overview of the main parts of Managed Runtime, it’s time to get hands-on! A good place to start is the [Push and Deploy Bundles](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/pushing-and-deploying-bundles.html) guide.

# Managed Runtime Overview

[Managed Runtime](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html) provides the infrastructure to deploy, host, and monitor your PWA Kit storefront.

:::important
Managed Runtime only supports applications created from a PWA Kit template. The source code for the available templates can be found in the `template-*` folders in the [PWA Kit repository](https://github.com/SalesforceCommerceCloud/pwa-kit/tree/develop/packages) on GitHub.
:::

This guide covers the main parts of Managed Runtime and how to access it.

::include{src="../../shared/managed-runtime-access.md"}

:::important
Before you can use Managed Runtime and Runtime Admin, ask your B2C Commerce administrator to add one of these roles to your account in Account Manager: **Managed Runtime User** or **Managed Runtime Admin**.
:::

## Environments

An **environment** is the term used to describe all of the cloud infrastructure and configuration values for a particular storefront hosted by Managed Runtime. Environments are used to separate your production storefront from other storefronts that are deployed for other purposes, such as development or testing.

:::note
In the [Managed Runtime API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=Summary), environments are called “targets,” but both terms refer to the same thing.
:::

Because environments run on highly efficient microservices that automatically scale up and down, you can create as many environments as you need at no additional cost. For example, you could create a short-lived environment dedicated to a single agile development sprint or for a single user story within that sprint. When you no longer need an environment, we encourage you to delete them.

### Production Environments

Environments marked as production are prioritized for monitoring by Salesforce’s Support team. For production environments, you can also [Debug Using Log Center](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/debugging.html#debug-using-log-center). To mark an environment as a production, you have two choices:

1. Use the Runtime Admin tool. Step-by-step instructions for creating an environment or editing an existing environment are found in the [Environments](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html#environments) section of the Administration guide.
2. Use the Managed Runtime API. The [projects_target_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_create) and [projects_target_partial_update](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_partial_update) endpoints both feature the `is_production` parameter. To mark an environment as production with these endpoints, set `is_production` to `true`.

:::important
By default, you can mark up to 10 environments as production. To increase your limit, contact Support.
:::

## Bundles

The storefront code that runs on an environment is called a **bundle**. Use the developer tools included in PWA Kit to generate a bundle and push it to Managed Runtime.

:::note
A bundle is a snapshot of your code at a specific point in time. It’s *immutable*: After a bundle has been created, it can’t be changed. Having this complete and accurate history of bundles makes troubleshooting deployments easier.
:::

After pushing the bundle, you can use the Runtime Admin or Managed Runtime API to designate that bundle as “deployed.” Each project can have multiple bundles, but each environment can have only one bundle that's designated as deployed. You can change which bundle is designated as deployed at any time. For more information, see [Push and Deploy Bundles](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/pushing-and-deploying-bundles.html).

## Projects and Organizations

To help you manage multiple environments, each environment also belongs to a **project** and each project belongs to an **organization**. An organization can contain multiple projects for multiple storefronts and each project can contain multiple environments. A Managed Runtime user can belong to multiple organizations to separate different work streams.

Each organization can have a maximum of 100 total environments and a maximum of 10 production environments. If you need to raise these limits, contact your Salesforce Support representative.

Organizations and user organization membership is determined by settings in Account Manager. A user can belong to an organization as either a member or an admin. Members can only interact with the projects in Managed Runtime that they’ve been assigned a project role to. Admins can interact with all the projects within an organization.

:::important
To assign a user the admin organization membership, contact Salesforce Support.
:::

## Users, Abilities, and Roles

All users must be assigned the `Managed Runtime User` or `Managed Runtime Admin` via [Account Manager](https://account.demandware.com) for accessing Managed Runtime.

### Organization Roles and Permissions

Any user can have the following capabilities for a Managed Runtime organization:

- **Browse:** View all projects for an Organization.
- **Certificate:** View or manage TLS Certificates for an organization.

### Project Roles and Permissions

Any user can have the following capabilities for a Managed Runtime project:

- **Browse:** View the project in Runtime Admin.
- **Manage Redirects:** Manage redirects for the project. Please review the [Redirects documentation](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html?q=Redirects#redirects) to learn more.
- **Deploy:** Deploy new bundles or revert the deployment to an older bundle.
- **Manage Team:** View, add, invite, remove, and edit the roles of team members for the project.
- **Access Logs:** Tail logs across all environments.
- **View and Manage Environment Variables:** See and manage environment variables in each environment. See [Environment Variables](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/environment-variables.html).

Each user is assigned a project role that determines which abilities they have. (A user can only have *one* role.) Project roles can be assigned to any user within an organization.

The following table shows which abilities are associated with each project role:

| Project Role | Browse | Manage Redirects | Deploy | Manage Team | Access Logs | View and Manage Environment Variables |
| :----------- | :----- | :--------------- | :----- | :---------- | :---------- | :------------------------------------ |
| Admin        | Yes    | Yes              | Yes    | Yes         | Yes         | Yes                                   |
| Developer    | Yes    | Yes              | Yes    | No          | Yes         | Yes                                   |
| Marketer     | Yes    | Yes              | No     | No          | No          | No                                    |
| Viewer       | Yes    | No               | No     | No          | No          | No                                    |

## App Server

Within each Managed Runtime environment, the [React](https://reactjs.org/) app in the published bundle runs inside a [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) environment. To respond to page requests and render the results, we use the [Express](https://expressjs.com/) web framework with the help of PWA Kit’s [rendering](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/rendering.html) and [routing](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/routing.html) systems. We call this combination of React, Node, and Express the **App Server**. (Although, technically speaking, the App Server runs on “serverless” technology.) The App Server is optimized to run on cloud infrastructure that offers low computing costs, high availability, fast rendering, and massive scaling capacity.

Because PWA Kit’s rendering and routing system handles the differences between local development environments and Managed Runtime environments, your code runs in a predictable way when you deploy it. This predictability unlocks your development team’s productivity by encouraging them to deploy bundles more frequently.

Currently, the App Server supports Transport Layer Security (TLS) versions 1.2 and greater.

### Environment Variables

Code running on the App Server has access to the following environment variables:

- `DEPLOY_TARGET`: ID of the environment.
- `EXTERNAL_DOMAIN_NAME`: The domain name set on the environment.
- `MOBIFY_PROPERTY_ID`: ID of the project that the environment belongs to.

## Edge Services

Supporting the app server are several edge services, including:

- A web application firewall (WAF) to protect your environments from attackers
- A proxy server to speed up API requests
- A content delivery network (CDN) to cache requests and speed up page loading
- Edge functions that process requests and handle redirects

The proxy server and CDN are covered in detail in our guide to [Proxying Requests](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/proxying-requests.html). The edge function called the request processor is covered in our guide to [Maximizing Your Cache Hit Ratio](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/maximizing-your-cache-hit-ratio.html).

Managed Runtime’s edge services are strategically distributed throughout our public cloud infrastructure. Each service is located as close to the user as possible for faster performance.

## Admin Tools

To manage the settings for your organizations, projects, environments, and bundles, we offer two different tools:

1. The [Managed Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/), a web-based UI.
2. The [Managed Runtime API](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references?meta=managed-runtime-api\:Summary), a REST API that offers the same functionality as the web-based tool and some additional capabilities.

Use the Runtime Admin tool for routine tasks, such as deploying a new code bundle to an environment. Use the API whenever you need programmatic control, such as automatically creating an environment as part of a continuous integration script.

The admin tools give you a self-serve way to configure many settings, including:

- Allowed IP addresses
- Allowed access control headers
- Currently deployed bundle
- Deployment region
- Proxies
- Redirects
- User permissions
- Production environment flag

Access to the admin tools is controlled with Account Manager roles and an API key. For continuous integration (CI) and continuous delivery (CD) processes, dedicated bot users with their own API keys are typically provisioned by your organization.

Fun fact: Like your storefront, the Runtime Admin tool is a headless React app that is deployed to Managed Runtime.

## Constraints

While building your storefront, keep the following constraints of Managed Runtime environments in mind:

### Environments

- Environments only respond to requests whose HTTP `Host` header matches their External Hostname set in Runtime Admin.
- The path `/` only accepts HTTP GET requests.
- Request and response size can’t exceed 6 MB.
- The maximum size of the HTTP request line and headers is 10240 bytes. Requests exceeding this size return an [HTTP 413 Content Too Large](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/413).
  - Of the 10,240 bytes, 1,500 bytes are reserved for internal use, 1,800 bytes for authorization headers, and 1,000 bytes for Salesforce B2C Commerce API (SCAPI). 5,940 bytes are left for custom request headers, including cookies.
- Cookies, including the HTTP request `Cookie` and HTTP response `Set-Cookie` header aren't supported by default. They can be enabled by setting the `allow_cookies` attribute on an environment with the [projects_target_partial_update](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_partial_update) endpoint. You can also enable cookies in the [Environment Settings](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html#edit-environment-settings) in [Runtime Admin](https://runtime.commercecloud.com/). Cookies are supported in PWA Kit version 3.1.0 or greater. See [Personalize with Cookies](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/personalize-with-cookies.html).
- Requests with headers that start with `_` are not supported. These requests will be dropped.
- HTTP requests originating from Managed Runtime environments don't use fixed IP addresses. To allow list requests from the App Server use the [AWS IP Range](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-ip-ranges.html) for `EC2`. To allow list requests from Proxies, use `CLOUDFRONT_ORIGIN_FACING`.
- The path prefix `/mobify` is reserved for managed endpoints. These endpoints include:
  - `/mobify/ping`: Returns an HTTP 200 response code when the environment is operating correctly.
  - `/mobify/redirect/$path`: Returns a similar response as [projects_target_redirect_retrieve](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_retrieve).
  - `/mobify/proxy/$name`: Returns a response from a [proxy](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/proxying-requests.html).
- You can bypass the CDN cache using the HTTP request header: `x-mobify-cachebreaker: 1`
- Environment IP Allowlists support up to 250 IP addresses. This limit can't be raised.
- Environment access control headers support up to 2 headers. Each header:
  - Can contain up to 128 characters.
  - Can be a combination of alphanumeric characters and - and \_ characters
  - See [Access Control Headers](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html#access-control-headers).

### Rendering

- The execution time for App Server requests is limited to 20 seconds for production environments and 16 seconds for non-production environments. After this time, an HTTP 502 is returned.
- Unhandled promise rejections break app rendering.

### Deployments

- The maximum size for bundles is 400 MB and the maximum size of all `ssr_only` and `ssr_shared` files within the bundle is 249 MB.
- Static assets that can be uploaded and served are limited to the following content types: `application/javascript`, `application/json`, `image/png` ,`image/gif`, `image/jpeg`, `image/svg+xml`, `image/webp`, `text/css`, `text/plain` and fonts (`ttf`, `woff`, `woff2`, `otf`, etc). All other content types need to be served by an external system.

### Proxies

Managed Runtime Proxies have different [constraints](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/guide/proxying-requests.html#constraints).

## Availability

You can subscribe to updates regarding the availability of Managed Runtime services on [Salesforce Status](https://status.salesforce.com/products/B2C_Commerce_Cloud).

## Next Steps

Now that you have an overview of the main parts of Managed Runtime, it’s time to get hands-on! A good place to start is the [Push and Deploy Bundles](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/pushing-and-deploying-bundles.html) guide.

::include{src="../../shared/managed-runtime-access.md"}

:::important
Before you can use Managed Runtime and Runtime Admin, ask your B2C Commerce administrator to add one of these roles to your account in Account Manager: **Managed Runtime User** or **Managed Runtime Admin**.
:::

## See Also

- [Managed Runtime Administration](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/managed-runtime-administration.html)
- [Managed Runtime API guide](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/using-the-managed-runtime-api.html)
- [Managed Runtime API reference](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=Summary)

After making your edits, click **Update** to save your changes or click **Cancel** to discard your changes. 439 440 ### Server-Side Rendering Architecture 441 442 Managed Runtime supports two processor architectures for Server-Side Rendering (SSR): ARM and x86. The architecture determines the underlying compute infrastructure used to render your storefront. 443 444 #### ARM Architecture (Default for New Projects) 445 446 ARM architecture is the default for all new projects created in Managed Runtime. ARM processors offer several advantages. 447 448 - **Enhanced Performance**: ARM architecture provides efficient processing capabilities optimized for modern web workloads. 449 - **Modern Infrastructure**: Built on the latest cloud computing technologies. 450 451 **Who Can Use It**: All new Managed Runtime projects automatically use ARM architecture. 452 453 #### x86 Architecture (Scheduled for Retirement) 454 455 :::warning 456 The x86 architecture is retiring on **January 31, 2027**. After that date, environments running on x86 can't be deployed. Environments aren't deleted and continue to respond to requests. Switch your environments to ARM before this date to avoid deployment disruptions. 457 ::: 458 459 The x86 architecture is available for existing customers until its retirement on January 31, 2027. 460 461 **Who**: Existing customers with projects created before ARM architecture was introduced can continue using x86 until January 31, 2027. 462 463 #### Choosing an Architecture 464 465 - **New Projects**: ARM architecture is automatically selected and is the recommended choice for all new projects. 466 - **Existing projects**: x86 architecture is retiring on January 31, 2027. Switch your environments to ARM before this date to avoid deployment disruptions. Admins can switch existing environments to ARM at any time in Runtime Admin under environment settings. Most projects require no code changes. If your project uses architecture-specific native modules, test in a non-production environment before switching production. 467 468 #### Project-Level Default Architecture 469 470 You can set a default architecture at the project level that automatically applies to all new environments created within that project. This setting streamlines environment creation by eliminating the need to select an architecture for each new environment. 471 472 How to Set Project-Level Default: 473 474 1. Go to a project's Overview page. 475 2. Click **Project Settings** from the left navigation. 476 3. Under **Environment Defaults** and **Server Architecture**, select either **ARM** or **x86**. 477 4. Click **Update**. 478 479 All new environments created in the project automatically use the selected default architecture. Existing environments aren't affected by changes to the project-level default. 480 481 ### Clear an Environment's CDN Cache 482 483 You can clear some or all of an environment's cached content in the content delivery network (CDN). Clearing the CDN cache helps to ensure that shoppers see the most recent and accurate version of content on your site. 484 485 Use the [projects_target_invalidation_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_invalidation_create) API to clear all cached content, specific URLs, or directories. 486 487 It's not possible to clear the CDN cache in Runtime Admin. However, when you redeploy a bundle, that clears all cached content for the associated environment. 488 489 :::note 490 Invalidation of the CDN cache temporarily results in slower performance for the first shoppers accessing the site after the invalidation. 491 ::: 492 493 ## Environment Variables 494 495 See [Environment Variables](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/environment-variables.html). 496 497 ## Access Control Headers 498 499 Access control headers allow you to restrict access to an environment so that only trusted traffic coming from your content delivery network (CDN) or development team is allowed. Restricting access is important to ensure that bots don't go around your CDN perimeter security settings and to ensure that search crawlers don’t index content from the wrong domain or environment. 500 501 If Allowed IP addresses are also set, requests with either a valid IP address or an access control header are allowed through. 502 503 ### Usage 504 505 Set access control headers by using the [Advanced Environment Settings](#edit-environment-settings) or the [projects_target_access_control_header_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_access_control_header_create) API. 506 507 Incoming requests are allowed only if an `x-sfdc-access-control` request header is present with a valid value. 508 509 ### Constraints 510 511 A header value is made up of your chosen set of characters. Each header value: 512 513 - Must be at least 9 characters long 514 - Can contain up to 128 characters 515 - Can be a combination of alphanumeric characters and `-` and `_` characters 516 517 Access control headers are not available to code running in a Managed Runtime environment. 518 519 ### Rotate Access Control Headers 520 521 You’re responsible for ensuring that the access control header value is securely stored and shared only with trusted individuals. We strongly recommend rotating the access control header on a regular basis. 522 523 To rotate an access control header: 524 525 - Add an access control header value to the Managed Runtime environment by using the [Advanced Environment Settings](#edit-environment-settings) or the [projects_target_access_control_header_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_access_control_header_create) API. 526 - Wait for the Environment redeploy to complete successfully. Verify requests to the environment with the new header value succeed with a command such as: 527 528 ```bash 529 curl https://myproject-mytarget.mobify-storefront.com/ -H "x-sfdc-access-control: 123456789" -o /dev/null 530 ``` 531 532 - Update your CDN or browser to send the `x-sfdc-access-control` request header with the updated value. 533 - Test that traffic is being allowed through as expected. 534 - Remove the original access control header value by using the [Advanced Environment Settings](#edit-environment-settings) or the [projects_target_access_control_header_create](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_access_control_header_create) API. 535 536 **See Also** 537 538 - [Configure Your Environment](/docs/commerce/b2c-commerce/guide/launching-your-storefront.html#5-configure-your-environment) 539 540 ## Redirects 541 542 A redirect allows you to forward a request from the requested URL to a different URL. Redirects can help avoid disruptions to the user experience caused by changes to your storefront. For example, consider a seasonal campaign page for spring. When the spring campaign ends and is replaced with a summer campaign, you can redirect from the spring URL to the summer URL. 543 544 Redirects is a powerful feature that can have significant security consequences on your storefront, including redirecting to malicious URLs or assets. Please be careful when assigning roles to your users that give them Redirect access. 545 546 ### Create a Redirect 547 548 :::tip 549 Before creating a redirect in a production environment, we recommend that you create it in a staging environment first. 550 ::: 551 552 You can also create one or more redirects using the [projects_target_redirect_create](/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_create) API endpoint. 553 554 To create a redirect using Runtime Admin: 555 556 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 557 2. Click the name of the environment where you want to create the redirect. 558 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 559 4. Click **Create Redirect**. 560 5. In the **Redirect From** field, enter a relative URL path. For example, to redirect visitors from the URL `www.example.com/winter`, enter `/winter`. 561 6. In the **Redirect To** field, enter a relative URL path. 562 7. If needed, enable forwarding of query parameters and the wildcard path. (More information on forwarding settings in a moment.) 563 8. From the **Redirect Type** dropdown menu, select a redirect type based on the HTTP status code. (More information on status codes in a moment.) 564 9. Click **Create Redirect**. 565 566 Let’s look at the options for creating a redirect in more detail. 567 568 #### Paths 569 570 The value that you enter in the **Redirect From** field must always be a *relative* path. The **Redirect To** field can be either a relative path or a full URL. For example, imagine that we want to redirect visitors from `www.example.com/spring` to `www.example.com/summer`. The **Redirect From** field must be `/spring`. The **Redirect To** field can be either `/summer` or `www.example.com/summer`. 571 572 #### Wildcards 573 574 You can add an asterisk character (`*`) to the end of the **Redirect From** URL to indicate a wildcard. A wildcard matches any (0 or more) characters in the URL. For example, a redirect from `/a/*` would match `/a/`, `/a/b`, and `/a/b/c`. 575 576 A wildcard character can only be used at the end of the **Redirect From** URL. 577 578 Standard redirects are processed first by Managed Runtime, followed by redirects with wildcards. 579 580 #### HTTP Status Codes 581 582 Most redirects use the Permanent 301 status code, but you can also select Temporary 302. If you’re unsure which HTTP status code to use, consult this [status code explainer](https://moz.com/learn/seo/redirection) from MOZ.com. 583 584 #### Forwarding Query Parameters 585 586 Some requests contain query string parameters that you also want to include in the redirected request. For example, the relative path `/spring-landing-page` can be appended with a query string for analytics tracking, such as `/spring-landing-page?gclid=123`. 587 588 To enable query parameter forwarding, go to the **Forward** section of the form and select **Query Parameters**. Otherwise, query string parameters from the source URL aren’t included in the redirect URL. 589 590 What happens when both the **Redirect From** and **Redirect To** URLs both have query strings and forwarding is enabled? In this case, the redirect URL includes a combination of the two query strings. The query parameters from the **Redirect To** URL are appended to the query string in the request. For example, imagine your application receives a request for the relative path `/spring?year=2019`. If you’ve chosen to redirect `/spring` to `/summer?year=2020`, the redirect URL is `/summer?year=2019&year=2020` when forwarding is enabled. 591 592 #### Forwarding Wildcard Path 593 594 You can automatically include any path that comes after the wildcard portion of the **Redirect From** URL in the **Redirect To** URL. For example: if `/a/*` matches `/a/b/c` in the **Redirect From** URL, and the **Redirect To** URL is `/z/`, the redirect URL is `/z/b/c`. 595 596 To enable wildcard path forwarding, go to the **Forward** section of the form and select **Wildcard Path**. 597 598 ### Clone Redirects 599 600 :::tip 601 We recommend that you always create redirects in a staging environment and clone them into production after testing them. 602 ::: 603 604 You can copy all the redirects from one environment to another using the clone redirects feature. 605 606 You can also clone redirects using the [projects_target_redirect_clone_create ](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_clone_create) API endpoint. 607 608 To clone redirects using Runtime Admin: 609 610 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 611 2. Click the name of the environment that contains the redirects that you want to clone. 612 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 613 4. Click **Clone Redirects**. The **Clone Redirects** form appears. The current environment is listed under **From Environment** (the source). 614 5. Under **To Environment**, select the environment that you want to clone the redirects into (the destination). 615 6. Click **Clone n Redirects**. (Where n is the number of redirects to be cloned.) 616 617 :::warning 618 When you clone redirects, you’re replacing *all* the redirects in the destination environment with *all* the redirects from the source environment. 619 ::: 620 621 ### Edit a Redirect 622 623 You can also edit a redirect using the [projects_target_redirect_partial_update](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_partial_update) API endpoint. 624 625 To edit the settings for an existing redirect using Runtime Admin: 626 627 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 628 2. Click the name of the environment that contains the redirect that you want to edit. 629 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 630 4. Click the ellipsis button (...) next to the redirect. 631 5. Click **Edit**. 632 6. Update the settings. 633 7. Click **Update Redirect**. 634 635 ### Delete a Redirect 636 637 You can also delete a redirect using the [projects_target_redirect_destroy](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/pwa-kit-managed-runtime/references/mrt-admin?meta=projects_target_redirect_destroy) API endpoint. 638 639 To delete a redirect using Runtime Admin: 640 641 1. Go to a project’s Overview page. 642 2. Click the name of the environment that contains the redirect that you want to delete. 643 3. Click **URL Redirects** from the left navigation. 644 4. Click the ellipsis button (...) next to the redirect. 645 5. Click **Delete**. 646 6. Click **Yes, Delete Redirect**. 647 648 ### Troubleshooting Redirects 649 650 If a redirect isn’t working as expected, try these troubleshooting steps: 651 652 - [Clear your browser cache](https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/32050?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop\&hl=en) because redirects are cached. 653 - Verify that you’re viewing the settings for the correct environment. 654 - Edit the redirect and verify that the correct values are entered in the **Redirect From** and **Redirect To** fields. 655 656 ### Technical Limitations with Redirects 657 658 Redirects have the following technical limitations: 659 660 - Each environment can have a maximum of 10,000 redirects. 661 - Each environment has its own set of redirects. It is your responsibility to keep them in sync using cloning. 662 - The redirects feature supports simple redirects from one path to another. For complex redirects with conditionals use Express.js' [redirects support](http://expressjs.com/en/api.html#res.redirect) in `ssr.js`. 663 - Redirects created with the Runtime Admin tool or the Managed Runtime API are not run on local development environments. 664 - Redirects are not triggered by page transitions in the PWA Kit application; they can only be triggered by an HTTP request. 665 - To load a redirect in the context of a storefront, use the managed endpoint `/mobify/redirect/$path`. 666 667 ## Users 668 669 Here’s how to manage your users. 670 671 ### Add a User 672 673 To add a user to a project: 674 675 1.
